title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄序
我
國家鄉試取士之法自兩京達之
天下無不同者然而考試官之
出于
上命監試官之由于臺選掌卷至對
讀官則吏部擇之巡綽及監門
===
官則總戎官擇之司提調者俱
先疏上
聞至期乃偕往供事若是者乃
兩京鄉試隆重之舊典非天下諸
藩鄉試所得而並焉者也若夫
三塲題目司提調者旣每次進
呈及試錄已成復率考試等官同
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄序

我國家鄉試取士之法，自兩京達之天下，無不同者。然而考試官之出于上命，監試官之由于臺選，掌卷至對讀官則吏部擇之，巡綽及監門官則總戎官擇之。司提調者俱先疏上聞，至期乃偕往供事。若是者，乃兩京鄉試隆重之舊典，非天下諸藩鄉試所得而並焉者也。若夫三塲題目，司提調者旣每次進呈，及試錄已成，復率考試等官同
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Our dynasty’s method of selecting men through the Provincial Examination is uniform, extending from the two capitals throughout the realm. Yet in the two capitals, Examiners receive imperial appointments, Examination Monitors are selected by the Censorate, officials from those responsible for handling examination papers to the Collators are selected by the Ministry of Personnel, and Patrol Officers and Gate Monitors are selected by the commander-in-chief. The Proctors first report all these appointments to the throne by memorial; when the appointed time arrives, the officials proceed together to perform their duties. Such are the longstanding arrangements that lend particular solemnity to the Provincial Examinations in the two capitals; the Provincial Examinations elsewhere in the realm cannot match them.

As for the questions for the three sessions, the Proctors submit them to the throne on each occasion. Once the examination record has been completed, they again lead the Examiners and other officials together …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
進呈于
丹陛之下至於放舉人之榜赴鹿
鳴之宴亦皆同時
聞奏而後退歸府涖事焉若是者則
惟順天鄉試爲然雖應天府亦
不得而並也
國家之所以優崇京邑而異待其
===
人士者固如是哉臣儲不肖前
弘治壬子巳忝順天府考試之
命今弘治辛酉八月壬子復忝與
侍講臣澯同被
命焉伏自惟念實有不任其兢惕
者翌日癸丑遂
陛辭以行迨入院門俛仰至公堂
punctuated:
進呈于丹陛之下。至於放舉人之榜、赴鹿鳴之宴，亦皆同時聞奏，而後退歸府涖事焉。若是者，則惟順天鄉試爲然，雖應天府亦不得而並也。國家之所以優崇京邑而異待其人士者，固如是哉！
臣儲不肖，前弘治壬子，巳忝順天府考試之命。今弘治辛酉八月壬子，復忝與侍講臣澯同被命焉。伏自惟念，實有不任其兢惕者。翌日癸丑，遂陛辭以行。迨入院門，俛仰至公堂
translation_en:
…present it before the vermilion steps of the throne. As for posting the list of provincial graduates and attending the Deer Calling Banquet, these too are reported to the throne at the appropriate time; only afterward do the officials withdraw and return to the prefectural offices to attend to their duties. Such procedures apply only to the Shuntian Provincial Examination; even Yingtian Prefecture cannot stand on an equal footing with it. Such indeed is the special honor the state accords the capital prefecture and the distinctive treatment it extends to its scholars!
Your unworthy servant Chu previously had the undeserved honor of appointment as Examiner for Shuntian Prefecture in the renzi year of Hongzhi [1492]. Now, on the renzi day of the eighth month of the xinyou year of Hongzhi [1501], I have again had the undeserved honor of receiving this appointment together with your servant Can, Expositor-in-Waiting. Humbly reflecting upon myself, I truly felt overwhelmed by apprehension. The following day, guichou, we took leave of Your Majesty at court and set out. When we entered the examination compound’s gate and looked about in the Hall of Utmost Impartiality…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
上則見夫棘牆板屋百爾具備
蓋府尹臣重府丞臣琦所以豫
為提調者有道矣防閑周慎內
外肅然蓋御史臣完臣崇熙所以
竭誠于監試者有道矣臣於此
復何求哉遂與臣澯及同考試
官臣聰等同入內簾精白供事
===
每命題之夕必瓣香上祝曰
國家將以此求賢才吾輩亦以此
圖報稱今所擬經書題目則取
其有傳註明白者曰無為以一
端之說而取人也嗟爾多士安
得沈潛經傳約文會理如吾前
輩諸君子者乎於詔誥論策表
punctuated:
上，則見夫棘牆板屋，百爾具備。蓋府尹臣重、府丞臣琦所以豫為提調者有道矣。防閑周慎，內外肅然，蓋御史臣完、臣崇熙所以竭誠于監試者有道矣。臣於此復何求哉？遂與臣澯及同考試官臣聰等同入內簾，精白供事。
每命題之夕，必瓣香上祝曰：「國家將以此求賢才，吾輩亦以此圖報稱。」今所擬經書題目，則取其有傳註明白者，曰：「無為以一端之說而取人也。」嗟爾多士，安得沈潛經傳，約文會理，如吾前輩諸君子者乎？於詔誥、論、策、表
translation_en:
…in the hall, we saw the thorn-topped walls and plank-built quarters, everything fully prepared. Clearly, your servants Zhong, the Prefect, and Qi, the Prefectural Vice Prefect, had carried out the advance arrangements with proper care. Precautions were thorough and scrupulous, and solemn order prevailed both inside and outside. Clearly, your servants Wan and Chongxi, the Censors, had devoted themselves wholeheartedly and properly to supervising the examination. What more could your servant ask for? Together with your servant Can and the Associate Examiners, including your servant Cong, I then entered the inner examination compound, serving with wholehearted purity of purpose.
On every evening when we set questions, we invariably offered incense and prayed: “Through this examination, the state seeks worthy talent; through it, we too seek to repay its favor fittingly.” In drafting questions on the Classics and the Four Books, we selected passages whose traditional expositions and commentaries were clear, saying: “Let us not select men on the basis of a one-sided interpretation.” Ah, you many scholars! How might we find among you those who immerse themselves deeply in the Classics and their commentaries, write concisely, and grasp their principles, as did the gentlemen of earlier generations? As for the topics for imperial proclamations and mandates, discourses, policy essays, and memorials…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
判題目則取其典故易知有關
於王體國論民生日用之常者
曰無爲以隱僻之說而困人也
又安得博雅不雜辭尚體要如
前輩諸君子者乎已而朝夕不
遑更相戒飭分房閱卷裁定去
留其中果有如所謂約文會理
===
辭尚體要者則喜且不寐持以
自賀曰是亦足多矣不知他日
施於官守言責者亦能如前輩
諸君子盡忠修職不自負其言
也哉間或有問於臣者曰諸生
皆誦法孔子其用志蓋高遠矣
今一則曰前輩二則曰前輩無
punctuated: 判題目，則取其典故易知、有關於王體國論、民生日用之常者，曰：「無爲以隱僻之說而困人也。」又安得博雅不雜、辭尚體要如前輩諸君子者乎？已而朝夕不遑，更相戒飭，分房閱卷，裁定去留。其中果有如所謂約文會理、辭尚體要者，則喜且不寐，持以自賀曰：「是亦足多矣！」不知他日施於官守言責者，亦能如前輩諸君子盡忠修職、不自負其言也哉？間或有問於臣者曰：「諸生皆誦法孔子，其用志蓋高遠矣。今一則曰前輩，二則曰前輩，無
translation_en:
… For the legal-judgment topics, we selected those whose historical precedents were readily understood and which concerned the principles of royal government, deliberations on affairs of state, and the ordinary needs of the people’s livelihoods and daily lives. We said: “Let us not trouble candidates with obscure and recondite matters.” And how might we find men who, like the gentlemen of earlier generations, possess broad and refined learning free of extraneous matter, and whose writing prizes substance and essentials?
Thereafter, allowing ourselves no respite morning or evening, we admonished one another, divided into rooms to read the papers, and decided which to reject and which to retain. Whenever we indeed found among them what we called concise expression that grasps principle, and writing that prizes substance and essentials, we were so delighted that we could not sleep. Holding up such papers, we congratulated ourselves, saying: “This, too, is worthy of high praise!” Yet I wonder whether, when these men later undertake the duties of office and the responsibility of remonstrance, they too will be able, like the gentlemen of earlier generations, to serve with utmost loyalty and discharge their duties, without belying their own words.
Occasionally someone would ask your servant: “The students all study and emulate Confucius; surely their aspirations are lofty and far-reaching. Yet now you speak of earlier generations at every turn—earlier generations this, earlier generations that. Is this not …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乃非所以進諸生於道乎臣以
爲不然何則前輩作事多周詳
後輩作事多闊略前輩多雅實
不爲華貌後輩則文過其質言
過其行浮譽過其實德邊幅過
其官理者多矣是豈憂
國家毗世道求有益於脩身治人
===
者所宜爾哉孔子忠信篤敬下
學而上達之道其殆且不如是
矣前輩之思不亦宜乎或者旣
以臣之言爲然臣故於序試錄
之末而倂及之蓋以見臣等區
區今日所以爲
國求賢勉圖報稱之意而亦以少
punctuated: 乃非所以進諸生於道乎？」臣以爲不然。何則？前輩作事多周詳，後輩作事多闊略；前輩多雅實，不爲華貌，後輩則文過其質、言過其行、浮譽過其實德、邊幅過其官理者多矣。是豈憂國家、毗世道、求有益於脩身治人者所宜爾哉？孔子忠信篤敬、下學而上達之道，其殆且不如是矣。前輩之思，不亦宜乎？或者旣以臣之言爲然，臣故於序試錄之末而倂及之，蓋以見臣等區區今日所以爲國求賢、勉圖報稱之意，而亦以少
translation_en:
…might this not fail to advance the students in the Way?” Your servant considers otherwise. Why? Those of the earlier generation generally acted with thoroughness and care; those of the later generation generally act with broad strokes and little attention to detail. The earlier generation generally possessed refinement and substance, without cultivating an ornate exterior. Among the later generation, many display more polish than substance, speak beyond what they put into practice, enjoy an empty reputation exceeding their actual virtue, and maintain outward appearances exceeding their competence in administering office. Is this fitting conduct for those who care for the state, support the moral order, and seek to make progress in cultivating themselves and governing others? Surely Confucius’s Way—being loyal and trustworthy, earnest and reverent, and advancing from learning below to understanding above—is not like this. Is it not appropriate, then, to look back to the earlier generation?

The questioner having accepted your servant’s words as sound, I have therefore also addressed this matter at the end of my preface to the examination record. This is to make manifest our humble intention, in seeking worthy men for the state today, to strive to render service commensurate with the favor we have received, and also, in some small measure, to…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
為諸士之勸也烏乎京邑天下
之表也京邑所貢人士亦天下
士之表也
國家平日之所為異待汝者其意
何在而何可不敬承懋勉以求
無愧於天下之士也哉主司相
屬望之心猶未可以一言而盡
===
也是為序
翰林院學士梁儲謹序
punctuated:
為諸士之勸也。烏乎！京邑天下之表也，京邑所貢人士亦天下士之表也。國家平日之所為異待汝者，其意何在？而何可不敬承懋勉，以求無愧於天下之士也哉！主司相屬望之心，猶未可以一言而盡也。是為序。
翰林院學士梁儲謹序。
translation_en:
…to offer encouragement to you scholars as well. Ah! The capital is the model for all under Heaven, and the scholars whom the capital recommends are likewise models for scholars throughout the realm. What is the intention behind the special treatment the state has customarily accorded you? How could you fail to receive it reverently and strive earnestly, seeking to stand without shame before the scholars of the realm? The hopes that the presiding examiners place in you cannot yet be fully expressed in a single statement. Thus I have written this preface.
Preface respectfully composed by Liang Chu 梁儲, Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
物有本末事有終始知所先後則近道矣
欲仁而得仁又焉貪
其爲氣也配義與道無是餒也
易
剛中而應行險而順
剛巽乎中正而志行柔皆順乎剛
天數二十有五地數三十凡天地之數五
===
十有五
復以自知恒以一德
書
勅天之命惟時惟幾
先王克謹天戒臣人克有常憲
志以道寧言以道接
惟民生厚因物有遷違上所命從厥攸好
爾克敬典在德
詩
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
物有本末，事有終始。知所先後，則近道矣。
欲仁而得仁，又焉貪？
其爲氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。

易
剛中而應，行險而順。
剛巽乎中正而志行，柔皆順乎剛。
天數二十有五，地數三十，凡天地之數五十有五。
復以自知，恒以一德。

書
勅天之命，惟時惟幾。
先王克謹天戒，臣人克有常憲。
志以道寧，言以道接。
惟民生厚，因物有遷；違上所命，從厥攸好。
爾克敬典，在德。

詩
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
Things have roots and branches; affairs have endings and beginnings. To know what should come first and what should come afterward is to be near the Way.
Desiring benevolence and obtaining benevolence, how could one be greedy?
As vital energy, it accords with righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
The firm occupies the central position and finds a response; moving through danger, it remains compliant.
The firm yields in centrality and correctness, and its purpose is carried out; the yielding all submit to the firm.
The numbers of Heaven total twenty-five, and the numbers of Earth total thirty; together, the numbers of Heaven and Earth total fifty-five.
Through Return, one knows oneself; through Constancy, one makes one's virtue steadfast.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
Diligently carry out Heaven's mandate, attending to the proper times and the first stirrings of events.
The former kings could heed Heaven's warnings, and their ministers could maintain constant standards.
Let your purposes be settled through the Way, and let your words be received in accordance with the Way.
The people are born with a generous nature, but change under the influence of things; they disregard what their superiors command and follow what they like.
Your ability to revere the established norms rests upon virtue.

Book of Odes (Shijing)

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
喓喓草蟲趯趯阜螽未見君子憂心忡忡
亦旣見止亦旣覯止我心則降
王命南仲往城于方出車彭彭旂旐央央
天子命我城彼朔方赫赫南仲獫狁于
襄
濟濟辟王左右趣之濟濟辟王左右奉璋
奉璋峩峩髦士攸宜淠彼涇舟烝徒楫
之周王于邁六師及之倬彼雲漢爲章
于天周王壽考遐不作人追琢其章金
===
玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四方
無競維人四方其訓之不顯維德百辟其
刑之於乎前王不忘
春秋
公及齊侯宋公陳侯衞侯鄭伯許男曹伯
會王世子于首止秋八月諸侯盟于
首止僖公五年
自十有二月不雨至于秋七月文公二年
會于蕭魚襄公十一年
punctuated:
喓喓草蟲，趯趯阜螽。未見君子，憂心忡忡。亦旣見止，亦旣覯止，我心則降。

王命南仲，往城于方。出車彭彭，旂旐央央。天子命我，城彼朔方。赫赫南仲，獫狁于襄。

濟濟辟王，左右趣之。濟濟辟王，左右奉璋。奉璋峩峩，髦士攸宜。淠彼涇舟，烝徒楫之。周王于邁，六師及之。倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人。追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。

無競維人，四方其訓之。不顯維德，百辟其刑之。於乎，前王不忘！

春秋

公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衞侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯，會王世子于首止。秋八月，諸侯盟于首止。僖公五年。

自十有二月不雨，至于秋七月。文公二年。

會于蕭魚。襄公十一年。
translation_en:
The grass insects chirp; the grasshoppers leap. Before I have seen my lord, my anxious heart is troubled. Once I have seen him, once I have met him, my heart is set at ease.

The king commanded Nan Zhong to go and build fortifications at Fang. The chariots went forth in great numbers, their banners splendidly displayed. “The Son of Heaven commands us to fortify that northern region.” Illustrious Nan Zhong drove out the Xianyun.

Dignified is the sovereign; those to his left and right hasten to serve him. Dignified is the sovereign; those to his left and right bear jade tablets. Majestic as they bear the tablets, these eminent men are well suited to their duties. The boats move upon the Jing River; the assembled men row them. The king of Zhou sets forth, and the six armies follow him. Brilliant is the Milky Way, forming a pattern in the heavens. The king of Zhou enjoys long life: does he not nurture men of talent? Their ornament is chased and carved; their substance is gold and jade. Tirelessly our king orders and governs the four quarters.

Strength beyond compare rests in worthy men: the four quarters will follow their instruction. How manifest is virtue: the many lords will take it as their model. Ah, the former kings are not forgotten!

Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the king’s heir apparent at Shouzhi. In autumn, in the eighth month, the regional lords made a covenant at Shouzhi. Fifth year of Duke Xi.

From the twelfth month there was no rain, continuing until the seventh month in autumn. Second year of Duke Wen.

They met at Xiaoyu. Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:

禮記
大臣法小臣廉官職相序君臣相正
德者性之端也樂者德之華也
上好是物下必有甚者矣故上之所好惡
不可不慎也
故事之盡禮樂而可數為以立德行者莫
若射故聖王務焉
===
第貳場

論治者貴識體

擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔文帝後元年
擬唐以宋璟為西京留守誥開元四年

德者，性之端也；樂者，德之華也。
上好是物，下必有甚者矣。故上之所好惡，不可不慎也。
故事之盡禮樂而可數為以立德行者，莫若射，故聖王務焉。

translation_en:
An autumn hunting muster was held at Hong. Eighth year of Duke Zhao.
A great hunting muster was held at Bipu. Eleventh year of Duke Zhao.
A great hunting muster was held at Changjian. Twenty-second year of Duke Zhao.

Record of Rites
The great ministers observe the rules; the lesser ministers maintain integrity. Officials rank in their proper order, and ruler and ministers correct one another.
Virtue is the upright expression of human nature; music is the flowering of virtue.
When those above favor something, there will certainly be those below who carry it further. Thus those above must exercise care in what they like and dislike.
Among activities that fully embody ritual and music and can be practiced repeatedly to establish virtuous conduct, none equals archery. Therefore the sage kings devoted themselves to it.

Second Session
Discourse
Those who discuss governance must value an understanding of its essential principles.

One question from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose, in the manner of the Han dynasty, an edict calling for deliberation on measures that could assist the common people. First year of Emperor Wen’s Later Era.
Compose, in the manner of the Tang dynasty, a proclamation appointing Song Jing as Regent of the Western Capital. Fourth year of Kaiyuan.
Compose, in the manner of the Song dynasty, a memorial of thanks for Kou Zhun’s appointment as Commissioner of Finance. Sixth year of Xianping.

Five Legal Judgments

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
人戶以籍爲定
禁止師巫邪術
孳生馬匹
修理橋梁道路
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問自昔制治之書雖周之周禮唐之六典
宋之會要元之經世大典亦不能久行
於當世豈其子孫不善於繼述而然耶
===
抑或以制作粗成未及修補致不能行
之於久遠而無弊也盍觀我
祖宗聖製之盛乎凡存心孝慈諸錄歷代君臣
諸鑑資世務本諸訓洪武聖政諸紀與
凡尚書會選孟子節文諸書俱藏之
內府有未易以寸晷而稱述者姑以諸士子
之所習聞者相與言之在
太祖時則有若
祖訓大誥禮制律令職掌憲綱官制諸書在
punctuated:
人戶以籍爲定。
禁止師巫邪術。
孳生馬匹。
修理橋梁道路。

第叄場
策〔五道〕

問：自昔制治之書，雖周之《周禮》、唐之《六典》、宋之《會要》、元之《經世大典》，亦不能久行於當世，豈其子孫不善於繼述而然耶？抑或以制作粗成，未及修補，致不能行之於久遠而無弊也？盍觀我祖宗聖製之盛乎？凡《存心》《孝慈》諸錄、歷代君臣諸鑑、《資世》《務本》諸訓、《洪武聖政》諸紀，與凡《尚書會選》《孟子節文》諸書，俱藏之內府，有未易以寸晷而稱述者。姑以諸士子之所習聞者，相與言之。在太祖時，則有若《祖訓》《大誥》《禮制》《律令》《職掌》《憲綱》《官制》諸書。在
translation_en:
Households shall be determined by their registration.
Prohibition of spirit mediums and sorcerers and their heterodox arts.
Breeding horses.
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: Among the books for ordering government from antiquity onward, even the Zhou dynasty’s Rites of Zhou, the Tang’s Six Compendia, the Song’s Collected Essentials, and the Yuan’s Great Compendium for Ordering the World could not remain in use for long under their respective dynasties. Was this because their descendants were unable to carry forward their predecessors’ work? Or was it because these institutions were only roughly established, and revisions and repairs were not made in time, so that they could not be implemented over the long term without defects? Why not consider the abundance of the sagely writings of our imperial ancestors?

The records on Preserving the Mind and on Filial Piety and Parental Kindness; the mirrors for rulers and ministers of successive dynasties; the instructions on Aiding the World and Attending to Fundamentals; the chronicles of the Sagely Government of the Hongwu Reign; and such books as the Collected Selections from the Book of Documents and the Abridged Mencius are all preserved in the inner palace repositories. They cannot readily be described in so brief a span of time. Let us therefore discuss those with which you candidates are familiar.

In the time of Taizu, there were such books as the Ancestral Instructions, the Grand Pronouncements, Ritual Institutions, Statutes and Ordinances, Official Responsibilities, Disciplinary Regulations, and the System of Official Posts. In…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
□宗時則有若爲善陰隲孝順事實五經四書
性理大全諸書在
宣宗
英宗
憲宗時則有若五倫書一統志續通鑑綱目諸
書是書也有藏之有司者矣有司則朝
夕奉行而弗懈有頒之學官臣庶者矣
臣庶則没身鑽仰而不及是豈無自而
致然耶願聞夫所以致然之道
===
問虞夏殷周之書吾夫子筆之而爲經先
秦漢晉隋唐諸書司馬公修之而爲通
鑑不知所謂經者其取義果何所自而
所謂鑑者其立名亦有所本耶六經之
後有作太玄以擬易者矣有假漢制以
續書者矣其取譬非不高也其於經也
有略相肖似者乎通鑑之後有别纂唐
事以示鑑戒者矣有補成舉要以適厥
中者矣其用意亦良勤也其於通鑑也
punctuated:
□宗時，則有若《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》《五經》《四書》《性理大全》諸書。在宣宗、英宗、憲宗時，則有若《五倫書》《一統志》《續通鑑綱目》諸書。是書也，有藏之有司者矣，有司則朝夕奉行而弗懈；有頒之學官臣庶者矣，臣庶則没身鑽仰而不及。是豈無自而致然耶？願聞夫所以致然之道。

問：虞夏殷周之書，吾夫子筆之而爲經；先秦漢晉隋唐諸書，司馬公修之而爲《通鑑》。不知所謂經者，其取義果何所自？而所謂鑑者，其立名亦有所本耶？六經之後，有作《太玄》以擬《易》者矣，有假漢制以續《書》者矣。其取譬非不高也，其於經也，有略相肖似者乎？《通鑑》之後，有别纂唐事以示鑑戒者矣，有補成《舉要》以適厥中者矣。其用意亦良勤也，其於《通鑑》也
translation_en:
…in the reign of □zong [?], there were such works as Doing Good and Hidden Merit, Accounts of Filial Obedience, and the comprehensive compilations on the Five Classics, the Four Books, and Human Nature and Principle. In the reigns of Xuanzong, Yingzong, and Xianzong, there were such works as the Book of the Five Relationships, the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm, and the Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror. Some of these books are kept by the responsible authorities, who put them into practice morning and evening without flagging. Others have been distributed to education officials, officials generally, and commoners, who study and revere them throughout their lives, yet cannot fully attain their teachings. Could this state of affairs have arisen without a cause? We wish to hear an explanation of how it came about.

Question: Our Master edited the writings of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou into a Classic; Lord Sima compiled the writings concerning pre-Qin times and the Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang into the Comprehensive Mirror. As for what is called a “Classic,” from precisely what does that designation derive its meaning? And does the name “Mirror” likewise have a foundation? After the Six Classics, someone composed the Supreme Mystery to emulate the Changes, and someone drew upon Han institutions to continue the Documents. The models they chose were certainly lofty; but do their works bear even some resemblance to the Classics? After the Comprehensive Mirror, someone separately compiled events of the Tang to provide examples and warnings, and someone supplemented and completed the Essentials to achieve a proper balance. Their intentions, too, were most painstaking; but in relation to the Comprehensive Mirror, …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有互相發明者乎說者以爲文公綱目
一書直可以上繼春秋之筆然綱目託
始於晉大夫爲諸侯之時而訖於宋藝
祖未登極之際大抵皆因通鑑之舊而
已非若春秋之創爲義例也今推尊綱
目而不及通鑑其意亦有所指耶或又
以爲綱目晚始成書朱子尚欲修補而
未及其提要所書與凡例多有不合者
故徐氏繼爲綱目考證以相補正今其
===
說故在不知其說亦有可取者否乎諸
生窮經觀鑑之餘於此必有成說幸相
與言之方今
聖明在
上時御
經筵尚書經傳久已進講而通鑑之與綱目
亦將以備用於他日凡我臣士固皆當
留意而預講焉者也諸生其毋多遜
問六經之道同歸而禮樂之用爲急班固
punctuated:
有互相發明者乎？說者以爲文公《綱目》一書，直可以上繼《春秋》之筆。然《綱目》託始於晉大夫爲諸侯之時，而訖於宋藝祖未登極之際，大抵皆因《通鑑》之舊而已，非若《春秋》之創爲義例也。今推尊《綱目》而不及《通鑑》，其意亦有所指耶？或又以爲《綱目》晚始成書，朱子尚欲修補而未及，其提要所書與凡例多有不合者，故徐氏繼爲《綱目考證》以相補正。今其說故在，不知其說亦有可取者否乎？諸生窮經觀鑑之餘，於此必有成說，幸相與言之。方今聖明在上，時御經筵，《尚書》經傳久已進講，而《通鑑》之與《綱目》亦將以備用於他日。凡我臣士，固皆當留意而預講焉者也。諸生其毋多遜！

問：六經之道同歸，而禮樂之用爲急。班固
translation_en:
…do they illuminate one another? Some maintain that the Outline and Details (Gangmu) by Master Wen, Zhu Xi, can indeed carry forward the historical writing of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Yet the Outline and Details takes as its starting point the time when the great officers of Jin became feudal lords, and ends just before the founding emperor of the Song ascended the throne. In broad terms, it merely follows the existing Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian); it does not establish interpretive principles and conventions anew as the Spring and Autumn Annals did. When people now exalt the Outline and Details without according the same recognition to the Comprehensive Mirror, do they have some particular point in mind?

Others maintain that the Outline and Details was completed only late in Zhu Xi’s life, and that he still wished to revise and supplement it but did not have time. What is written in its summaries often fails to accord with its general editorial principles. Accordingly, Master Xu subsequently composed the Textual Investigations of the Outline and Details (Gangmu kaozheng) to supplement and correct it. His explanations are still extant; is there anything in them worth adopting? You students, in the course of your thorough study of the Classics and reading of the Mirror, must have arrived at considered views on these matters. Please share them.

At present, our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above and regularly attends the Classics Colloquium. The text and commentaries of the Book of Documents have long been expounded before him, and the Comprehensive Mirror and the Outline and Details will also be held ready for use in the future. All of us, his officials and scholars, should certainly give these works our attention and study them in advance. You students should not be overly modest!

Question: The Way of the Six Classics leads to the same end, but the practical application of rites and music is the most urgent. Ban Gu…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有是言也不知所謂急者其義果安在
三代治出於一而禮樂達於天下歐陽
脩有是言也不知所謂達者其道當何
如夫禮陰而樂陽禮先而樂後固也然
禮之節文度數尚可以援據而言樂之
聲氣性情則未易以心思而得何孔子
之時夏殷之禮已不足徵而季札使魯
乃能審知夫先世之樂耶漢唐以来其
英君誼辟有志於禮樂者亦衆矣然而
===
冠昏喪祭飲射讀法居室器服之禮迄
未能達之于天下而郊廟社稷山川百
神朝會燕饗之樂率不足以傳之于来
裔何耶我
太祖高皇帝在位餘三十年治定而功成制禮
而作樂凡禮之所以辨上下而定民志
樂之所以媲雅頌而和神人者
聖子神孫固已世守而勿失矣夫何邇年以来
有司之禮制稍不行士庶之奢僭浸無
punctuated: 有是言也，不知所謂急者，其義果安在？三代治出於一，而禮樂達於天下，歐陽脩有是言也，不知所謂達者，其道當何如？夫禮陰而樂陽，禮先而樂後，固也。然禮之節文度數，尚可以援據而言；樂之聲氣性情，則未易以心思而得。何孔子之時，夏殷之禮已不足徵，而季札使魯，乃能審知夫先世之樂耶？漢唐以来，其英君誼辟有志於禮樂者亦衆矣。然而冠昏喪祭、飲射讀法、居室器服之禮，迄未能達之于天下；而郊廟社稷、山川百神、朝會燕饗之樂，率不足以傳之于来裔，何耶？我太祖高皇帝在位餘三十年，治定而功成，制禮而作樂。凡禮之所以辨上下而定民志，樂之所以媲雅頌而和神人者，聖子神孫固已世守而勿失矣。夫何邇年以来，有司之禮制稍不行，士庶之奢僭浸無
translation_en:
…made this statement. What, precisely, is meant by calling them urgent? “Under the Three Dynasties, government issued from a single source, and rites and music extended throughout the realm”: Ouyang Xiu made this statement. By what means should this extension be achieved? That rites belong to yin and music to yang, and that rites come first and music follows, is certainly so. Yet the prescribed forms, measures, and numbers of rites can still be discussed with reference to evidence, whereas the sounds and vital energies, innate dispositions and emotions of music are not easily grasped through reflection. Why was it that, in Confucius’s time, evidence for the rites of Xia and Yin was already insufficient, yet Jizha, when sent on a mission to Lu, could discern the music of earlier ages so accurately? Since the Han and Tang, there have been many illustrious rulers and righteous sovereigns devoted to rites and music. Nevertheless, the rites of capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, communal drinking, archery, public reading of the laws, dwellings, utensils, and dress have never been extended throughout the realm. And the music for the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices, the altars of Soil and Grain, the mountains and rivers and the hundred spirits, court assemblies, and banquets has generally proved unworthy of transmission to later generations. Why is this?
Our Emperor Taizu Gao reigned for more than thirty years. Once his government was firmly established and his achievements complete, he instituted rites and composed music. All the means by which rites distinguish superiors from inferiors and give the people’s aspirations a settled direction, and by which music matches the Odes and Hymns and brings spirits and human beings into harmony, have indeed been preserved without loss, generation after generation, by his sagely sons and divine grandsons. Why, then, have the ritual regulations administered by the responsible officials gradually fallen into disuse in recent years, while extravagance and the usurpation of distinctions of rank among scholars and commoners have increasingly become without…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
度今日禁之明日逾甚其傷財妨政之
害誠尤有甚於天災者今
聖明在上側身修行勤恤民隱方舉行救災恤
患之典有司於此而不加禁絕焉夫豈
所以上承
德意節用而裕民之道也哉我諸生其推本
三王禮樂之原究後代禮樂不興之故
詳我
朝禮樂刑政四達不悖之實而直言今日之
===
所當禁者冀具以聞之於
上無隱辭焉
問道學之傳必有師友開其端門人接其
緒而後斯道明於世若宋之諸儒輩出
先後一轍何其盛哉夫程子之學出自
濂溪而或者乃比諸橫渠之遇范文正
何以辨其說歟朱子之學嘗稟於籍溪
屏山而學者乃直以繼延平之統何以
知其然歟程子之所與游者張橫渠□
punctuated:
度，今日禁之，明日逾甚，其傷財妨政之害，誠尤有甚於天災者。今聖明在上，側身修行，勤恤民隱，方舉行救災恤患之典。有司於此而不加禁絕焉，夫豈所以上承德意、節用而裕民之道也哉？我諸生其推本三王禮樂之原，究後代禮樂不興之故，詳我朝禮樂刑政四達不悖之實，而直言今日之所當禁者，冀具以聞之於上，無隱辭焉。

問：道學之傳，必有師友開其端，門人接其緒，而後斯道明於世。若宋之諸儒輩出，先後一轍，何其盛哉！夫程子之學出自濂溪，而或者乃比諸橫渠之遇范文正，何以辨其說歟？朱子之學嘗稟於籍溪、屏山，而學者乃直以繼延平之統，何以知其然歟？程子之所與游者，張橫渠□
translation_en:
…beyond all bounds. Prohibit it today, and tomorrow it grows still worse. The harm it causes by wasting resources and impeding government is indeed even greater than that of natural disasters. Now our sagely and enlightened ruler reigns above, humbly cultivating his conduct and diligently attending to the people's hidden sufferings, and is putting into effect measures to relieve disasters and alleviate distress. If the responsible officials fail to prohibit and eradicate these practices, how can this be the way to uphold his benevolent intentions, economize on expenditure, and enrich the people? You candidates should trace the origins of rites and music under the Three Kings, investigate why rites and music failed to flourish in later ages, and explain fully how our dynasty's rites, music, punishments, and government operate everywhere without conflict. Speak plainly about what ought to be prohibited today. We hope to submit your views in full to His Majesty; conceal nothing in your words.

Question: For the Learning of the Way to be transmitted, teachers and friends must initiate it, and disciples must carry on its thread; only then can this Way become manifest in the world. Consider how the Confucian scholars of the Song arose in succession, those before and after following the same course. How flourishing it was! Master Cheng's learning originated with Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi], yet some compare this to Hengqu [Zhang Zai]'s encounter with Fan Wenzheng [Fan Zhongyan]. How can their claim be assessed? Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] once received instruction from Jixi [Hu Xian] and Pingshan [Liu Zihui], yet scholars simply regard him as continuing the lineage of Yanping [Li Tong]. How can we know that this is so? Those with whom Master Cheng associated were Zhang Hengqu and □ [?]…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
堯夫耳然一則主禮以敎人一則主數
而觀物不知於程子之學果有合乎否
也朱子之所與學者張南軒呂伯恭耳
然一則論仁而不合一則論史記而不
合不知於朱子之道亦有同乎否也程
子之門人多矣有天資穎悟者有德宇
溫粹者有英果明决强力不倦者有修
身好學深潜縝密者而卒傳其道者誰
歟朱子之門人衆矣有造詣純篤者有
===
學知根據者有精識博聞推明易學者
有潜心書範闡發幽微者而深得其傳
者誰歟夫程朱所傳皆孔子之道也而
其有功於聖門孰爲大其所以爲學之
方孰爲要然而程子門人乃有流於禪
學者亦獨何哉是必有說矣試言之以
觀志道之學
問結繩之後人文旣作而字書出焉是蓋
國家生民之不可一日無者也□□之
punctuated:
堯夫耳。然一則主禮以敎人，一則主數而觀物，不知於程子之學果有合乎否也？朱子之所與學者，張南軒、呂伯恭耳。然一則論仁而不合，一則論史記而不合，不知於朱子之道亦有同乎否也？程子之門人多矣，有天資穎悟者，有德宇溫粹者，有英果明决、强力不倦者，有修身好學、深潜縝密者，而卒傳其道者誰歟？朱子之門人衆矣，有造詣純篤者，有學知根據者，有精識博聞、推明易學者，有潜心書範、闡發幽微者，而深得其傳者誰歟？夫程朱所傳，皆孔子之道也，而其有功於聖門孰爲大？其所以爲學之方孰爲要？然而程子門人乃有流於禪學者，亦獨何哉？是必有說矣。試言之，以觀志道之學。
問：結繩之後，人文旣作，而字書出焉。是蓋國家生民之不可一日無者也。□□之
translation_en:
…Yaofu, and no others. Yet one emphasized ritual in teaching others, while the other emphasized numbers in observing things. Did their approaches actually accord with Master Cheng’s learning? Those with whom Master Zhu pursued learning were Zhang Nanxuan and Lü Bogong, and no others. Yet with one he disagreed in discussing benevolence, and with the other he disagreed in discussing the Records of the Grand Historian. Did their approaches nevertheless share anything with Master Zhu’s Way? Master Cheng had many disciples: some were naturally perceptive; some had a warm and pure moral disposition; some were outstandingly resolute, clear in judgment, and tireless in effort; and some cultivated themselves, loved learning, and were deeply reflective and meticulous. But who ultimately transmitted his Way? Master Zhu had numerous disciples: some were pure and steadfast in their attainments; some possessed well-grounded learning and understanding; some combined keen discernment with broad knowledge and elucidated the study of the Changes; and some devoted themselves to the “Great Plan” of the Book of Documents, bringing its obscure subtleties to light. But who deeply grasped his transmitted teachings? What Masters Cheng and Zhu transmitted was in each case the Way of Confucius. Which made the greater contribution to the tradition of the Sage? What was most essential in their methods of learning? Yet some of Master Cheng’s disciples drifted into Chan Buddhist learning. Why was this so? There must surely be an explanation. Set it forth, so that we may assess your learning directed toward the Way.
Question: After the era of knotted cords, human culture arose, and writings on characters appeared. These are surely things that the state and its people cannot do without for even a single day. Of □□ [?] …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
權輿肇自蒼頡而或謂黃帝之先已有
字書文與字書本一物也或謂三者雖
同而各有取義六書之名起於何時條
分而縷析雖毛穎不能述也可舉其槩
而言歟六者之中或又分為三耦或又
有先後相承之序亦不可不知也蒼頡
之字謂之古文至周秦時有大篆小篆
隸書不知何人所作其於古文亦有合
歟又其後也有八分書楷書正書行書
===
章草飛白諸體則其去古益遠矣然亦
有可取者歟雖然此特字體之變也至
於後世承訛襲舛既久偏傍點畫不分
而字體亦失其眞矣我
太祖高皇帝創治之初命儒臣取許氏說文參
以毛晃註釋勒成洪武正韻一書頒行
天下凡於字之從俗字之所非字之疑
誤莫不校讎而歸正於是四海同文六
書復古矣然傳習既久苟簡漸生竊謂
punctuated: 權輿肇自蒼頡，而或謂黃帝之先已有字。書、文與字，書本一物也，或謂三者雖同而各有取義。六書之名起於何時？條分而縷析，雖毛穎不能述也，可舉其槩而言歟？六者之中，或又分為三耦，或又有先後相承之序，亦不可不知也。蒼頡之字謂之古文，至周秦時有大篆、小篆、隸書，不知何人所作？其於古文亦有合歟？又其後也，有八分書、楷書、正書、行書、章草、飛白諸體，則其去古益遠矣，然亦有可取者歟？雖然，此特字體之變也。至於後世承訛襲舛既久，偏傍點畫不分，而字體亦失其眞矣。我太祖高皇帝創治之初，命儒臣取許氏《說文》，參以毛晃註釋，勒成《洪武正韻》一書，頒行天下。凡於字之從俗、字之所非、字之疑誤，莫不校讎而歸正。於是四海同文，六書復古矣。然傳習既久，苟簡漸生，竊謂
translation_en:
…its beginnings originated with Cangjie, yet some say that characters already existed before Huangdi. Writing (shu), graphic forms (wen), and characters (zi)—writing is fundamentally one thing [?]; others say that although the three are alike, each term conveys a distinct meaning. When did the designation “Six Principles of Writing” (liushu) arise? To distinguish their categories and analyze every detail would exceed even the powers of Mao Ying, the writing brush. Can you state their broad outlines? Some further divide these six into three pairs; others arrange them in a sequence in which each follows from the preceding one. These matters, too, must be understood.

Cangjie’s characters are called “ancient script.” By the Zhou and Qin periods there were large seal script, small seal script, and clerical script. Who created them? Do they have anything in common with ancient script? Subsequently there appeared such styles as eight-part script, standard script, regular script, running script, clerical cursive, and flying-white script. These departed increasingly far from antiquity, yet might they also have merits? Nevertheless, these are merely changes in the forms of characters. As later generations perpetuated errors over a long period, failing to distinguish character components, dots, and strokes, the forms of characters also lost their authenticity.

At the beginning of his rule, our Emperor Taizu Gao commanded his scholarly officials to take Xu’s Explanation of Graphs and Analysis of Characters (Shuowen), consult Mao Huang’s annotations, and compile the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu Zhengyun), which was promulgated throughout the realm. Characters following popular usage, characters deemed incorrect [?], and doubtful or erroneous characters were all collated and corrected. Thus all within the Four Seas shared a common writing system, and the Six Principles of Writing were restored to their ancient form. Yet, as its transmission and study continued over time, careless shortcuts gradually arose. I venture to suggest that…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
今之府史胥徒亦知遵式而經生儒士
或反不達其故何也願明言之以懲不
恪
punctuated: 今之府史胥徒亦知遵式，而經生儒士或反不達其故，何也？願明言之，以懲不恪。
translation_en: …even today’s clerks, scribes, runners, and attendants know to follow the prescribed forms, yet students of the Classics and scholars sometimes fail to understand the reasons behind them. Why is this? Please explain clearly, so as to admonish those who fail to observe them conscientiously.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人一百三十五名
第一名謝丕浙江餘姚縣人監生禮記
第二名李錫順天府東安縣學生詩
第三名趙祜直隸長垣縣學增廣生易
第四名張愈江西南城縣人監生春秋
第五名許瓛順天府學附學生書
第六名李廷相順天府學附學生詩
第七名魏境順天府學附學生易
===
第八名馬允中直隸鉅鹿縣學生詩
第九名張宜錦衣衛官籍監生書
第十名劉廷芳直隸蠡縣學生詩
第十一名孫經直隸開州學生易
第十二名高振直隸廣平府學生詩
第十三名米璟順天府學附學生書
第十四名閔槐直隸任丘縣學增廣生詩
第十五名殷秀錦衣衛軍餘易
第十六名徐天澤順天府學附學生禮記
punctuated:
中式舉人一百三十五名。

第一名謝丕，浙江餘姚縣人，監生，禮記。
第二名李錫，順天府東安縣學生，詩。
第三名趙祜，直隸長垣縣學增廣生，易。
第四名張愈，江西南城縣人，監生，春秋。
第五名許瓛，順天府學附學生，書。
第六名李廷相，順天府學附學生，詩。
第七名魏境，順天府學附學生，易。
第八名馬允中，直隸鉅鹿縣學生，詩。
第九名張宜，錦衣衛官籍，監生，書。
第十名劉廷芳，直隸蠡縣學生，詩。
第十一名孫經，直隸開州學生，易。
第十二名高振，直隸廣平府學生，詩。
第十三名米璟，順天府學附學生，書。
第十四名閔槐，直隸任丘縣學增廣生，詩。
第十五名殷秀，錦衣衛軍餘，易。
第十六名徐天澤，順天府學附學生，禮記。
translation_en:
Successful provincial graduates (juren): 135 in total.

First: Xie Pi, a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education. His examination classic was the Record of Rites.
Second: Li Xi was a student of the Dong’an County School, Shuntian Prefecture. His examination classic was the Classic of Poetry.
Third: Zhao Hu was an added-quota student of the Changyuan County School, Zhili. His examination classic was the Classic of Changes.
Fourth: Zhang Yu, a native of Nancheng County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
物有本末事有終始知所先後則近道矣
趙祜
同考試官訓導趙批於知所先後處體認親切
而詞亦溫雅可法是用錄出
同考試官教諭周批此題似易而實難意足者文
繁言簡者理晦明淨可錄者僅見此篇
考試官侍講張批詞整潔而意涵蓄大學義當如是矣
===
考試官學士梁批自起承至歸結處皆有可取者
大學有自然之序爲學有入道之方夫本末始
終大學自然之序不可紊也學者求入道焉舎
知序其奚以哉經文此節結上文兩節之意以
爲明德之當明也在己民德之當新也在人明
德之與新民固兩物也兩物而內外相對則內
者是其本而外者是其末矣謂不有本末乎惟
能先知其所止然後能得其所止知止之與能
得固一事也一事而首尾相因則首者是其始
punctuated:
第一場
四書
「物有本末，事有終始，知所先後，則近道矣。」
趙祜
同考試官訓導趙批：「於知所先後處體認親切，而詞亦溫雅可法，是用錄出。」
同考試官教諭周批：「此題似易而實難，意足者文繁，言簡者理晦，明淨可錄者僅見此篇。」
考試官侍講張批：「詞整潔而意涵蓄，《大學》義當如是矣。」
考試官學士梁批：「自起承至歸結處，皆有可取者。」
《大學》有自然之序，爲學有入道之方。夫本末始終，《大學》自然之序，不可紊也。學者求入道焉，舎知序，其奚以哉？經文此節，結上文兩節之意，以爲明德之當明也在己，民德之當新也在人。明德之與新民，固兩物也。兩物而內外相對，則內者是其本，而外者是其末矣，謂不有本末乎？惟能先知其所止，然後能得其所止。知止之與能得，固一事也。一事而首尾相因，則首者是其始
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“Things have roots and branches; affairs have endings and beginnings. Knowing what should come first and what should come after brings one near the Way.”

Zhao Hu

Associate Examiner Zhao, Assistant Instructor, comments: “His understanding of knowing what should come first and what should come after is intimate and precise. His language, too, is gentle and refined, worthy of emulation. For these reasons, this essay has been selected for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “This topic seems easy but is actually difficult. Those who fully develop its meaning write at excessive length; those whose language is concise obscure its principles. This is the only essay I have seen that is clear and lucid enough to merit inclusion.”

Examiner Zhang, Expositor, comments: “The language is orderly and polished, while the meaning is rich in implication. An exposition of the meaning of the Great Learning should indeed be like this.”

Examiner Liang, Academician, comments: “From the opening and its development through to the conclusion, every part has something commendable.”

The Great Learning has a natural sequence; pursuing learning has a method for entering the Way. Roots and branches, beginnings and endings constitute the natural sequence of the Great Learning, which must not be confused. If students seek to enter the Way, how can they do so without knowing this sequence? This section of the classic draws together the meaning of the two preceding sections: the luminous virtue that must be illuminated lies within oneself, while the virtue of the people that must be renewed lies in others. Illuminating luminous virtue and renewing the people are indeed two things. When these two things are set against each other as inward and outward, the inward is the root and the outward the branches. Can one say that there are no roots and branches?

Only by first knowing where to rest can one then attain that resting place. Knowing where to rest and being able to attain it are indeed one affair. Within this single affair, the head and tail are linked in dependence upon each other; thus the head is its beginning…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而末者是其終矣謂不有終始乎夫物有本末
則當先其本而後其末事有終始則當先其始
而後其終為大人之學者誠能知夫本之所當
先而不以末之當後者先之則明德可明民德
可新其道固可以循序而漸進矣夫豈遠乎哉
誠能知夫始之所當先而不以終之當後者越
之則知止可求能得可至其道固可以得門而
漸入矣又豈遠乎哉以是言之則知止者固止
於至善之由而知所先後者又為知止之由矣
===
大學以此結上文兩節之意其示人也夫豈不
深切而著明也哉抑觀此節既總結上文兩節
之意下文即以其綱領之條目詳言之蓋脩身
以上明明德之事也齊家以下新民之事也物
格知至則知所止矣意誠以下則皆得所止之
序也說者謂三綱領實統乎八條目八條目實
隸乎三綱領又謂此節先後二字實起下文先
後十二字其義理精密如此此其所以為經文
也歟
punctuated:
而末者是其終矣，謂不有終始乎？夫物有本末，則當先其本而後其末；事有終始，則當先其始而後其終。為大人之學者，誠能知夫本之所當先，而不以末之當後者先之，則明德可明，民德可新，其道固可以循序而漸進矣。夫豈遠乎哉？誠能知夫始之所當先，而不以終之當後者越之，則知止可求，能得可至，其道固可以得門而漸入矣。又豈遠乎哉？以是言之，則知止者固止於至善之由，而知所先後者又為知止之由矣。《大學》以此結上文兩節之意，其示人也，夫豈不深切而著明也哉？
抑觀此節既總結上文兩節之意，下文即以其綱領之條目詳言之。蓋脩身以上，明明德之事也；齊家以下，新民之事也。物格知至，則知所止矣；意誠以下，則皆得所止之序也。說者謂三綱領實統乎八條目，八條目實隸乎三綱領；又謂此節先後二字，實起下文先後十二字。其義理精密如此，此其所以為經文也歟？
translation_en:
…and the last is its end. Can one say that there are no ends and beginnings? Since things have roots and branches, one should put their roots first and their branches afterward; since affairs have ends and beginnings, one should put their beginnings first and their ends afterward. If those pursuing the learning of the great person truly understand that the root must come first, and do not give precedence to the branches that ought to follow, then luminous virtue can be made manifest and the people’s virtue can be renewed. Along this Way, they can indeed advance gradually in the proper sequence. How could it be far away? If they truly understand that the beginning must come first, and do not leap past it to the end that ought to follow, then knowing where to rest can be sought and attaining that resting place can be achieved. They can indeed find the gateway to this Way and enter gradually. Again, how could it be far away? Viewed in this light, knowing where to rest is certainly the means of resting in the highest good, while knowing what comes first and what comes afterward is in turn the means of knowing where to rest. The Great Learning uses this passage to conclude the meaning of the two preceding sections. Is its instruction not profound, pertinent, clear, and manifest?
Furthermore, observe that, after this section sums up the meaning of the two preceding sections, the text that follows immediately explains it in detail through the particular steps belonging to its guiding principles. Cultivating the person and the steps preceding it concern making luminous virtue manifest; regulating the family and the steps following it concern renewing the people. When things have been investigated and knowledge has reached its fullest extent, one knows where to rest. Making the intentions sincere and all the subsequent steps constitute the sequence by which one attains that resting place. Commentators say that the three guiding principles indeed encompass the eight steps, and that the eight steps indeed fall under the three guiding principles. They also say that the two characters meaning “first” and “afterward” in this section introduce the twelve occurrences of those characters in the text that follows. Its meaning and principles are so finely articulated and exact: is this not why it constitutes the canonical text?

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
欲仁而得仁又焉貪
許獻
同考試官訓導林批講欲仁處不以政事附會其
說蓋篤實之士也故用錄之
同考試官教諭楊批作者多體認仁字不真失
之穿鑿發揮明暢殆無如此篇者
考試官侍講張批不為題所窘可嘉
考試官學士梁批不求甚異中自有好處
惟所欲自足乎善則所欲不傷於廉此君子從
===
政之美也夫善之可欲莫大於仁也君子欲仁
而得仁則足乎己而無事外求矣又何貪之為
害哉昔聖人以五美荅子張問政而及此謂夫
君子之心未嘗無欲也而自有不害其為欲者
存是故天下之物凡有利于人者皆可欲矣而
君子之所欲則惟在於仁焉天下之欲凡其繫
于物者不可必得矣而君子之欲仁則未嘗不
得焉蓋仁者心之全德也吾於一日之間而欲
吾仁則全德即此而在初不待勉強而後得也
punctuated:
欲仁而得仁，又焉貪？
許獻
同考試官訓導林批：講欲仁處，不以政事附會其說，蓋篤實之士也，故用錄之。
同考試官教諭楊批：作者多體認仁字不真，失之穿鑿；發揮明暢，殆無如此篇者。
考試官侍講張批：不為題所窘，可嘉。
考試官學士梁批：不求甚異，中自有好處。
惟所欲自足乎善，則所欲不傷於廉，此君子從政之美也。夫善之可欲，莫大於仁也。君子欲仁而得仁，則足乎己而無事外求矣，又何貪之為害哉？昔聖人以五美荅子張問政，而及此，謂夫君子之心未嘗無欲也，而自有不害其為欲者存。是故天下之物，凡有利于人者，皆可欲矣；而君子之所欲，則惟在於仁焉。天下之欲，凡其繫于物者，不可必得矣；而君子之欲仁，則未嘗不得焉。蓋仁者，心之全德也。吾於一日之間而欲吾仁，則全德即此而在，初不待勉強而後得也。
translation_en:
“He desires benevolence and obtains benevolence: how, then, could he be greedy?”
Xu Xian

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: In explaining the desire for benevolence, he does not force his interpretation into a connection with governmental affairs. He is evidently a sincere and substantial scholar; therefore I selected this essay for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Most writers fail truly to grasp the meaning of benevolence and fall into strained interpretations. For lucid and fluent exposition, scarcely any essay equals this one.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: He is not hemmed in by the topic. Commendable.

Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: Without striving for extraordinary novelty, the essay has merits of its own.

Only when what one desires finds its fulfillment in goodness does that desire leave one’s integrity unimpaired. This is an excellence of the gentleman in conducting government. Among desirable forms of goodness, none is greater than benevolence. When the gentleman desires benevolence and obtains it, he finds sufficiency within himself and has no need to seek anything outside. How, then, could greed do him harm?

In former times, when the Sage answered Zizhang’s question about government by speaking of the five excellences, he touched upon this point. His meaning was that the gentleman’s heart is never without desires, yet there are desires that may remain desires without causing harm. Thus, of all things under Heaven, whatever benefits people may be desired; yet what the gentleman desires lies solely in benevolence. Of all desires under Heaven, those attached to external things cannot be certain of fulfillment; yet the gentleman’s desire for benevolence never fails to be fulfilled.

For benevolence is the complete virtue of the heart. If, within the course of a single day, I desire benevolence in myself, that complete virtue is present here and now. Its attainment never depends upon first forcing myself to act.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
仁者心之正理也吾於一事之頃而求吾仁則
正理即此而存初不假智力而後得也取之於
己而無愧所謂心廣體胖是已得之以道而自
足所謂優游饜飫是已欲仁而得仁如此又何
貪之足累乎蓋仁之可欲本出於自然而貪之
爲弊實生于多欲彼人情於可好之物固有以
非道而得之者以非道得之則縱欲敗度而不
免爲貪矣人情於可嗜之利固有以非義而取
之者以非義取之則貪得無厭而害其爲廉矣
===
今焉取吾固有之善而一毫不預於人是欲以
德而不以物也雖富所有庸何傷求吾本然之
性而一介無取於人是欲以道而不以利也雖
恣所得夫何害欲而不貪如此以之從政則政
無不立以之臨民而民豈有不被其澤者哉抑
考此章夫子因子張問從政而告以尊五美屏
四惡旣舉其綱而又著其目論語之告問政未
有如此之備者也故弟子記之終篇以繼帝王
之治焉由是而觀則夫子之爲政可知矣惜乎
punctuated: 仁者，心之正理也。吾於一事之頃而求吾仁，則正理即此而存，初不假智力而後得也。取之於己而無愧，所謂心廣體胖是已；得之以道而自足，所謂優游饜飫是已。欲仁而得仁如此，又何貪之足累乎？蓋仁之可欲，本出於自然，而貪之爲弊，實生于多欲。彼人情於可好之物，固有以非道而得之者；以非道得之，則縱欲敗度而不免爲貪矣。人情於可嗜之利，固有以非義而取之者；以非義取之，則貪得無厭而害其爲廉矣。今焉取吾固有之善，而一毫不預於人，是欲以德而不以物也；雖富所有，庸何傷？求吾本然之性，而一介無取於人，是欲以道而不以利也；雖恣所得，夫何害？欲而不貪如此，以之從政，則政無不立；以之臨民，而民豈有不被其澤者哉？抑考此章，夫子因子張問從政而告以尊五美、屏四惡，旣舉其綱，而又著其目。《論語》之告問政，未有如此之備者也。故弟子記之終篇，以繼帝王之治焉。由是而觀，則夫子之爲政可知矣。惜乎！
translation_en:
Benevolence is the proper principle of the heart. If, in the course of a single undertaking, I seek my own benevolence, that proper principle is present here and now; its attainment does not depend on intellectual ingenuity or force. To draw it from oneself without shame is what is meant by “the heart is broad and the body at ease.” To attain it through the Way and find sufficiency in oneself is what is meant by “dwelling at ease in full satisfaction.” When one desires benevolence and attains it in this way, how could greed encumber one?

That benevolence is desirable arises from what is natural, whereas the harm of greed truly arises from excessive desires. In their feelings toward attractive things, people sometimes obtain them by means contrary to the Way. Obtaining them thus, they indulge their desires and violate proper bounds, and inevitably become greedy. In their feelings toward tempting gains, people sometimes take them by means contrary to righteousness. Taking them thus, they become insatiable in acquisition and compromise their integrity.

Now, to draw upon the goodness inherently one's own without involving others in the slightest is to direct desire toward virtue rather than material things. However abundant one's possessions, what harm could there be? To seek one's original nature without taking the least thing from others is to direct desire toward the Way rather than profit. However freely one attains what one seeks, what harm could there be? To desire without greed is like this. Apply it in government, and no undertaking will fail to be established; apply it in governing the people, and could any fail to receive its benefits?

Furthermore, examining this chapter, we find that when Zizhang asked about serving in government, the Master instructed him to honor the five excellent practices and banish the four evils. Having set forth the main principles, he also specified their particulars. Among the answers to questions about government in the Analects, none is so comprehensive as this. Therefore his disciples recorded it in the final chapter, to carry forward the governance of the emperors and kings. Viewed in this light, the Master's approach to government can be understood. Alas! …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
□□少仁而不足以進於此也噫
其爲氣也配義與道無是餒也
李錫
同考試官教諭任批講配道義處不泛不略本
房孟子義此其最優者矣
同考試官教諭楊批作者於配字類能言至餒
字便窘手理明詞暢無如此篇
同考試官教諭胡批融會傳註成文不費詞而
意自足豈嘗究心於理學者歟
===
考試官侍講張批說理文字如此停當者亦少
考試官學士梁批明淨可錄
大賢論浩然之氣必言其得養而充失養而歉
也夫氣一而已矣充之則配乎道義而有餘不
充則反之吾身而不足氣其可失養乎哉昔者
公孫丑問浩然之氣孟子答之至此意以謂至
大至剛者乃是氣浩然之本體塞乎天地者亦
是氣浩然之功用顧人之所以養之者善否何
如耳誠能直養無害使氣之至大者不虧自反
punctuated:
□□少仁，而不足以進於此也。噫！

「其爲氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。」
李錫

同考試官教諭任批：講配道義處，不泛不略，本房孟子義，此其最優者矣。
同考試官教諭楊批：作者於配字類能言，至餒字便窘手。理明詞暢，無如此篇。
同考試官教諭胡批：融會傳註成文，不費詞而意自足，豈嘗究心於理學者歟？
考試官侍講張批：說理文字如此停當者亦少。
考試官學士梁批：明淨可錄。

大賢論浩然之氣，必言其得養而充、失養而歉也。夫氣一而已矣，充之則配乎道義而有餘，不充則反之吾身而不足。氣其可失養乎哉？昔者公孫丑問浩然之氣，孟子答之，至此意以謂：至大至剛者，乃是氣浩然之本體；塞乎天地者，亦是氣浩然之功用。顧人之所以養之者，善否何如耳。誠能直養無害，使氣之至大者不虧，自反
translation_en:
…□□ deficient in benevolence [?], and unable to advance to this. Alas!

“As vital energy, it accords with righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves.”
Li Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor: His discussion of how vital energy accords with the Way and righteousness is neither vague nor cursory. Of the essays on the Mencius assigned to this examining section, this is the finest.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Writers generally have something to say about the word “accords,” but become hampered when they reach the word “starves.” For clarity of principle and fluency of expression, none equals this essay.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: He integrates the commentaries into a coherent composition, fully conveying his meaning without wasting words. Might he be someone who has devoted himself to the Learning of Principle?

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: Few compositions explaining principles are so well judged as this.

Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: Clear and clean; worthy of inclusion.

When the great worthy discusses the vast, flowing vital energy, he necessarily explains that it becomes full when nourished and deficient when deprived of nourishment. Vital energy is, after all, a single thing. Fill it, and it accords with the Way and righteousness, with abundance to spare; fail to fill it, and, examining ourselves, we find it insufficient. Can vital energy be left unnourished?

Formerly, Gongsun Chou asked about the vast, flowing vital energy. When Mencius reached this point in his reply, his meaning was this: being supremely great and supremely firm constitutes the fundamental nature of this vast, flowing vital energy; filling Heaven and Earth is likewise its functioning. It depends only on whether people nourish it well. If one can truly nourish it with uprightness without harming it, so that its supreme greatness suffers no diminution, and examine oneself…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而縮使氣之至剛者不失則其道義之存乎心
者旣足以為一身之主而是氣之充乎體者又
足以為道義之助由是當行而行無所顧慮凡
可以行義而達道者沛然莫之能禦也非是氣
有以合而助之歟為之勇决無所疑憚凡可以
由義而盡道者浩乎不可復遏也非是氣有以
輔而翼之歟氣之得其養者如此使或不知有
事素無直養之功有所作為重為是氣之害則
本雖至大也今則有所限量矣何至大之有本
===
雖至剛也今則可以屈撓矣何至剛之有由是
一時所為雖未必不出於道義也然氣之在體
者已不充則將疑懼之不暇安望其振拔而有
為耶一事所行雖未必遽違乎道義也然氣之
在我者已不足則將顧望之不遑安望其奮厲
而有執耶是則養氣之功其有關於吾身道義
者如此又安可不盡其善養之道也哉抑合此
章而觀之公孫丑疑孟子當大任而動心孟子
遂極言知言養氣之功丑又疑知言養氣之旣
punctuated: 而縮，使氣之至剛者不失，則其道義之存乎心者旣足以為一身之主，而是氣之充乎體者又足以為道義之助。由是當行而行，無所顧慮，凡可以行義而達道者，沛然莫之能禦也，非是氣有以合而助之歟？為之勇决，無所疑憚，凡可以由義而盡道者，浩乎不可復遏也，非是氣有以輔而翼之歟？氣之得其養者如此。使或不知有事，素無直養之功，有所作為，重為是氣之害，則本雖至大也，今則有所限量矣，何至大之有？本雖至剛也，今則可以屈撓矣，何至剛之有？由是一時所為，雖未必不出於道義也，然氣之在體者已不充，則將疑懼之不暇，安望其振拔而有為耶？一事所行，雖未必遽違乎道義也，然氣之在我者已不足，則將顧望之不遑，安望其奮厲而有執耶？是則養氣之功，其有關於吾身道義者如此，又安可不盡其善養之道也哉？抑合此章而觀之，公孫丑疑孟子當大任而動心，孟子遂極言知言養氣之功。丑又疑知言養氣之旣
translation_en:
…and find oneself upright, so that the utmost firmness of one's qi is not lost, then the Way and righteousness present in the heart are sufficient to govern one's whole person, while the qi filling the body is also sufficient to assist the Way and righteousness. Thus one acts when action is called for, without hesitation or misgiving. Whatever serves to practice righteousness and realize the Way proceeds with a surging force that none can resist. Is this not because qi joins with them and lends assistance? One acts courageously and decisively, without doubt or fear. Whatever serves to follow righteousness and fulfill the Way advances with a vast force that can no longer be checked. Is this not because qi supports and sustains them? Such is qi when properly nourished.

If, however, one does not understand that there must be continual application, ordinarily makes no effort to nourish qi through uprightness, and, when acting, further harms this qi, then, although it is originally of the utmost greatness, it now has limits. Where is its utmost greatness? Although originally of the utmost firmness, it can now be bent and broken. Where is its utmost firmness? Consequently, although what one does on a particular occasion may indeed spring from the Way and righteousness, if the qi within the body is no longer full, one will be wholly occupied with doubt and fear. How can one expect to rouse oneself and accomplish anything? Although a particular action may not immediately violate the Way and righteousness, if the qi within oneself is already insufficient, one will be wholly occupied with hesitation and looking about for guidance. How can one expect to exert oneself resolutely and hold firmly to one's purpose? Such is the bearing that the work of nourishing qi has upon the Way and righteousness within oneself. How, then, could one fail to pursue fully the proper means of nourishing it?

Now, considering this chapter as a whole, Gongsun Chou suspected that Mengzi would be disturbed in mind when entrusted with great responsibilities. Mengzi therefore explained at length the work of understanding words and nourishing qi. Chou further wondered whether understanding words and nourishing qi already…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖孟子遂極言夫子之聖之盛要之夫子之聖
不假乎養氣知言而孟子之養氣知言乃學而
至聖者也先儒謂孟子此章擴前聖所未發學
者宜潛心而玩索不其然乎
易
剛中而應行險而順
趙祜
同考試官訓導趙批發明丈人行師之善貫通切
實易義之最優者也歆羡歆羡
===
同考試官教諭周批用師之道備在易書此作
既發揮明悉至結題處尤論證不苟其殆有見之士乎
考試官侍講張批詞氣嚴密是真知丈人之德者
考試官學士梁批講行險而順一句比他卷為勝
丈人行師之善於卦之體德見之焉蓋剛中而
應行險而順行師之至善者也卦之體德如是
非丈人而克爾耶吾夫子傳師之彖而推原丈
人吉无咎之義謂夫為將過剛則威懷無法在
上無應則信任不專以此行師殆難乎其有濟
punctuated:
聖，孟子遂極言夫子之聖之盛。要之，夫子之聖不假乎養氣知言，而孟子之養氣知言，乃學而至聖者也。先儒謂孟子此章擴前聖所未發，學者宜潛心而玩索，不其然乎？

易
剛中而應，行險而順。
趙祜

同考試官訓導趙批：發明丈人行師之善，貫通切實，易義之最優者也。歆羡，歆羡！
同考試官教諭周批：用師之道，備在易書。此作既發揮明悉，至結題處，尤論證不苟，其殆有見之士乎？
考試官侍講張批：詞氣嚴密，是真知丈人之德者。
考試官學士梁批：講行險而順一句，比他卷為勝。

丈人行師之善，於卦之體德見之焉。蓋剛中而應，行險而順，行師之至善者也。卦之體德如是，非丈人而克爾耶？吾夫子傳師之彖，而推原丈人吉无咎之義，謂夫為將，過剛則威懷無法，在上無應則信任不專，以此行師，殆難乎其有濟。
translation_en:
…sage. Mencius then spoke fully of the greatness of the Master's sagehood. In essence, the Master's sagehood did not depend upon nurturing his vital force and understanding words, whereas Mencius's nurturing of his vital force and understanding of words constituted attaining sagehood through learning. Earlier Confucian scholars said that this chapter of Mencius develops what previous sages had left unexplained, and that students should devote themselves to pondering and exploring it. Is this not so?

Book of Changes
“Firm and central, with a corresponding response; proceeding amid danger, yet compliant.”
Zhao Hu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Assistant Instructor: “This elucidates the excellence of the mature man's conduct of an army. Coherent and grounded in practical realities, it is the finest of the essays on the meaning of the Changes. Admirable, admirable!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The way to employ an army is fully set forth in the Book of Changes. This composition expounds it clearly and thoroughly; its argument and supporting evidence are particularly rigorous where it brings the topic to a conclusion. Surely its author is a man of insight!”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: “The language and tenor are rigorous and closely reasoned. This is someone who truly understands the virtue of the mature man.”

Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: “Its explanation of the phrase ‘proceeding amid danger, yet compliant’ surpasses that of the other papers.”

The excellence of the mature man's conduct of an army is manifest in the hexagram's structure and virtues. For being firm and central, with a corresponding response, and proceeding amid danger, yet compliant, constitute the highest excellence in conducting an army. Such are the hexagram's structure and virtues: could anyone other than a mature man achieve this? In commenting upon the Judgment of the Army hexagram, our Master traced the underlying meaning of ‘For a mature man, good fortune and no blame.’ His meaning was that, when serving as a general, excessive firmness leaves one without a proper method for inspiring awe and winning allegiance; without a corresponding response from above, one does not enjoy undivided trust and authority. To conduct an army in this manner would make success very difficult…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣師之卦體則不然九二以剛居下而用事六
五以柔居上而任之是剛中而應也剛中而應
則威惠並行士卒用命閫外之事將實專之連
百萬之衆而分數益明全勝之謀素定也承三
錫之恩而主心攸屬上下之交素固也行師之
善見於卦體者如此求其可以當此者其惟丈
人能然乎且兵之所在至險藏焉不以順動何
以除害以此行師亦難乎其有終吉矣師之卦
德則不然內體坎也而其德爲險外體坤也而
===
其德爲順是行險而順也行險而順則兵雖凶
器以順而動則不爲凶戰雖危事以順而動則
不爲危以之而禁暴除亂固无非順人心之事
也以之而攘外安內固无非順人情之舉也行
師之善見於卦德者又如此求其可以當此者
又非丈人能然乎吁丈人之才德如此則毒民
而民從之矣此其所以吉无咎也歟大抵用師
之道不徒以任將爲先而□以得正爲本此大
易所以有師貞丈人吉无咎之戒也後世有好
punctuated: 矣。師之卦體則不然：九二以剛居下而用事，六五以柔居上而任之，是剛中而應也。剛中而應，則威惠並行，士卒用命，閫外之事，將實專之。連百萬之衆而分數益明，全勝之謀素定也；承三錫之恩而主心攸屬，上下之交素固也。行師之善見於卦體者如此，求其可以當此者，其惟丈人能然乎？且兵之所在，至險藏焉，不以順動，何以除害？以此行師，亦難乎其有終吉矣。師之卦德則不然：內體坎也，而其德爲險；外體坤也，而其德爲順，是行險而順也。行險而順，則兵雖凶器，以順而動則不爲凶；戰雖危事，以順而動則不爲危。以之而禁暴除亂，固无非順人心之事也；以之而攘外安內，固无非順人情之舉也。行師之善見於卦德者又如此，求其可以當此者，又非丈人能然乎？吁！丈人之才德如此，則毒民而民從之矣。此其所以吉无咎也歟！大抵用師之道，不徒以任將爲先，而□以得正爲本，此大易所以有「師貞，丈人吉，无咎」之戒也。後世有好
translation_en:
…indeed. The structure of the hexagram The Army (Shi), however, is otherwise. The nine in the second place, firm and occupying a lower position, directs affairs; the six in the fifth place, yielding and occupying the higher position, entrusts him with responsibility. This is firmness centered and finding a response. With firmness centered and finding a response, authority and kindness operate together, the soldiers obey commands, and the general exercises sole authority over affairs beyond the palace gates. Even when assembling a host of a million, its organization and divisions remain all the clearer: plans for complete victory have been settled beforehand. Receiving the favor of three grants, he enjoys his ruler’s wholehearted trust: the bond between superior and subordinate has been secured beforehand. Such is the excellence in commanding an army revealed in the hexagram’s structure. If we seek someone equal to this, surely only a venerable man can achieve it?

Moreover, wherever arms are employed, the utmost danger lies concealed. Unless one acts in accordance with what is right, how can one eliminate harm? To command an army in this way would likewise make a fortunate outcome difficult. Yet the qualities of the hexagram The Army are otherwise. Its inner trigram is Kan, whose quality is danger; its outer trigram is Kun, whose quality is compliance. This is to proceed amid danger while remaining compliant. Proceeding amid danger while remaining compliant means that, although weapons are instruments of ill omen, employing them in accordance with what is right makes them no longer inauspicious; although warfare is a dangerous undertaking, conducting it in accordance with what is right makes it no longer perilous. Using such means to restrain violence and quell disorder is assuredly always in accord with the people’s hearts. Using them to repel external threats and secure peace within is assuredly always in accord with the people’s feelings. Such, again, is the excellence in commanding an army revealed in the hexagram’s qualities. If we seek someone equal to this, is it not again a venerable man who can achieve it?

Ah! With talents and virtue such as these, the venerable man may impose hardship upon the people, yet they will follow him. Is this not why there is good fortune and no blame? In general, the way of employing an army does not merely give priority to appointing a general; it □ takes attaining correctness as its foundation [?]. This is why the great Book of Changes offers the admonition: “The army must be correct; for a venerable man there is good fortune and no blame.” In later ages there were those who were fond of…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
大喜功无故而加兵於遠者其豈知師貞之戒
耶委用非人致有如霸上棘門之兒戲者其豈
知丈人吉无咎之戒耶噫大禹徂征方叔元老
後世殆邈乎其寡儔矣求其次者如漢之用周
亞夫趙充國唐之用李靖郭子儀數人者於大
易垂戒之義尚庶幾其不悖乎
天數二十有五地數三十凡天地之數五
十有五
魏境
===
同考試官訓導趙批此作本河圖自然之數
而發揮之殆經生中之表表者是可錄矣
同考試官教諭周批作此題者類欠明白此篇
善分析且无冗長語故錄之
考試官侍講張批以理演數之文潔淨無疵
考試官學士梁批講義明白結題亦有所見
大傳於河圖之數既分竒耦而積之復總竒耦
而計之蓋天地之數陽竒陰耦也大傳既分而
積之又總以計之則河圖全數之妙於是而見
punctuated:
大喜功，无故而加兵於遠者，其豈知師貞之戒耶？委用非人，致有如霸上棘門之兒戲者，其豈知丈人吉无咎之戒耶？噫！大禹徂征，方叔元老，後世殆邈乎其寡儔矣！求其次者，如漢之用周亞夫、趙充國，唐之用李靖、郭子儀，數人者於大易垂戒之義，尚庶幾其不悖乎？
天數二十有五，地數三十，凡天地之數五十有五。
魏境
同考試官訓導趙批：此作本河圖自然之數而發揮之，殆經生中之表表者，是可錄矣。
同考試官教諭周批：作此題者類欠明白，此篇善分析，且无冗長語，故錄之。
考試官侍講張批：以理演數之文，潔淨無疵。
考試官學士梁批：講義明白，結題亦有所見。
大傳於河圖之數，既分竒耦而積之，復總竒耦而計之。蓋天地之數，陽竒陰耦也。大傳既分而積之，又總以計之，則河圖全數之妙於是而見。
translation_en:
…grandeur and delight in achievements, launching military campaigns against distant lands without cause—how could such rulers understand the admonition that an army must act with correctness? Those who entrust command to unsuitable men, producing childish displays like those at Bashang and Jimen—how could they understand the admonition, “With a mature leader, good fortune; no blame”? Alas! The campaigning of Yu the Great and the venerable statesman Fang Shu have scarcely found their equals in later ages! If we seek men of the next rank, there are Zhou Yafu and Zhao Chongguo, employed by the Han, and Li Jing and Guo Ziyi, employed by the Tang. Did these few men not come close to fulfilling the meaning of the admonitions handed down in the great Book of Changes?
“The numbers of Heaven total twenty-five; the numbers of Earth total thirty. Together, the numbers of Heaven and Earth total fifty-five.”
Wei Jing
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Assistant Instructor: This composition takes the natural numbers of the River Chart as its basis and develops their meaning. Its author surely stands out among students of the classics. This merits inclusion.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Those who write on this topic generally lack clarity. This essay analyzes it well and contains no prolix wording; hence its inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: A composition that expounds numbers through principle, clean and free of flaws.
Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: The exposition of meaning is clear, and the conclusion also offers insight.
In treating the numbers of the River Chart, the Great Commentary first separates the odd and even numbers and adds them up, then combines the odd and even numbers to calculate their total. For among the numbers of Heaven and Earth, yang numbers are odd and yin numbers are even. The Great Commentary first separates and adds them, then combines them to calculate the total; thus the subtle significance of the River Chart’s full complement of numbers becomes apparent.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
奈何則天地之間一氣行而陰陽分陰陽分而
五行具河圖之為數不過一陰一陽一竒一耦
以兩其五行而已是故天以陽之輕清而位乎
上也陽數惟竒故圖之一三五生數也七與九
成數也皆以竒而屬之天焉五竒以五而積之
其為數也二十有五天之數不外乎是矣地以
陰之重濁而位乎下也陰數惟耦故圖之二與
四生數也六八十成數也皆以耦而屬之地焉
五耦以五而積之其為數也則有三十地之數
===
不越乎是矣夫天數之二十有五所以主變而
以生以成者也必合地數之三十而後化地數
之三十所以主化而克生克成者也必合天數
之二十有五而後變合天地之數總五十有五
統竒耦之積妙圖數之全于是陰陽配而五行
兩至理寓而大化存流行不滯變化无端所以
綱紀造化而顯著妙用也歟大傳發明以著大
衍之原其旨深哉抑論龍馬出河伏羲遂其文
以畫卦固也何係辭所論作易之由不一邪夫
punctuated: 奈何？則天地之間，一氣行而陰陽分，陰陽分而五行具。河圖之為數，不過一陰一陽、一竒一耦，以兩其五行而已。是故天以陽之輕清而位乎上也，陽數惟竒，故圖之一三五，生數也；七與九，成數也，皆以竒而屬之天焉。五竒以五而積之，其為數也二十有五，天之數不外乎是矣。地以陰之重濁而位乎下也，陰數惟耦，故圖之二與四，生數也；六八十，成數也，皆以耦而屬之地焉。五耦以五而積之，其為數也則有三十，地之數不越乎是矣。夫天數之二十有五，所以主變而以生以成者也，必合地數之三十而後化；地數之三十，所以主化而克生克成者也，必合天數之二十有五而後變。合天地之數，總五十有五，統竒耦之積，妙圖數之全。于是陰陽配而五行兩，至理寓而大化存，流行不滯，變化无端，所以綱紀造化而顯著妙用也歟！大傳發明，以著大衍之原，其旨深哉！抑論龍馬出河，伏羲遂其文以畫卦，固也。何係辭所論作易之由不一邪？夫
translation_en:
…How is this so? Between Heaven and Earth, a single vital energy circulates and differentiates into yin and yang; with this differentiation, the Five Phases are fully constituted. The numbers of the River Chart amount to no more than yin and yang, odd and even, providing a pair for each of the Five Phases. Thus Heaven occupies the position above through the lightness and purity of yang. Yang numbers are odd: hence, in the chart, one, three, and five are generating numbers, while seven and nine are completing numbers. All belong to Heaven because they are odd. Adding the five odd numbers together yields twenty-five; the numbers of Heaven do not extend beyond this. Earth occupies the position below through the heaviness and turbidity of yin. Yin numbers are even: hence, in the chart, two and four are generating numbers, while six, eight, and ten are completing numbers. All belong to Earth because they are even. Adding the five even numbers together yields thirty; the numbers of Earth do not exceed this.

Heaven’s numerical total of twenty-five governs change and thereby generates and completes things; only when it joins Earth’s total of thirty can transformation occur. Earth’s numerical total of thirty governs transformation and is thereby able to generate and complete things; only when it joins Heaven’s total of twenty-five can change occur. Combining the numbers of Heaven and Earth gives fifty-five in all, uniting the sums of odd and even and encompassing the wonder of the chart’s complete numerical scheme. Thus yin and yang are matched, and each of the Five Phases is paired; ultimate principle resides therein, and the great process of transformation subsists. Its circulation never stagnates, and its changes and transformations have no limit. Is this not how the creative process is ordered and its wondrous operation made manifest? The Great Commentary elucidates this to reveal the source of the Great Expansion. How profound its meaning is!

Now, as for the account that the dragon-horse emerged from the Yellow River and Fuxi followed its markings to draw the trigrams, that is certainly so. Why, then, does the Commentary on the Appended Statements give more than one explanation for the making of the Book of Changes? Now, …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
鴻荒之世天地陰陽雖各有象然數初未有也
至於河圖之出然後五十有五之數奇耦生成
粲然可見所以深發聖人之獨智非汎然物象
可得而擬也然伏羲仰觀俯察安知河圖非其
中之一事耶先儒謂聖人作易其法象之規模
必有最親切處其河圖之謂也
書
勅天之命惟時惟幾
許瓛
===
同考試官訓導林批題本冠冕作者多襲舊
文令人厭觀此篇詞嚴義正得虞廷警策臣工氣象可嘉
同考試官教諭楊批詞氣溫雅筆力雄健形容保
治之意殆盡允宜高薦
考試官侍講張批聖君憂勤惕厲之心摹寫近之
考試官學士梁批講時幾二字不戾本旨
欲有以致嚴於天當有以致慎於己蓋天命不
在人事外也然則欲致嚴於天命者惡可不自
時幾而致其謹哉帝舜將作歌而先述其所以
punctuated:
鴻荒之世，天地陰陽雖各有象，然數初未有也。至於河圖之出，然後五十有五之數，奇耦生成，粲然可見，所以深發聖人之獨智，非汎然物象可得而擬也。然伏羲仰觀俯察，安知河圖非其中之一事耶？先儒謂聖人作易，其法象之規模必有最親切處，其河圖之謂也。

書
勅天之命，惟時惟幾。
許瓛

同考試官訓導林批：題本冠冕，作者多襲舊文，令人厭觀。此篇詞嚴義正，得虞廷警策臣工氣象，可嘉。
同考試官教諭楊批：詞氣溫雅，筆力雄健，形容保治之意殆盡，允宜高薦。
考試官侍講張批：聖君憂勤惕厲之心，摹寫近之。
考試官學士梁批：講時幾二字，不戾本旨。

欲有以致嚴於天，當有以致慎於己，蓋天命不在人事外也。然則欲致嚴於天命者，惡可不自時幾而致其謹哉？帝舜將作歌，而先述其所以
translation_en:
…In remote antiquity, heaven and earth, yin and yang, each had their manifestations, but numbers had not yet appeared. Only with the emergence of the River Chart did the fifty-five numbers, their odd and even groupings, and their relations of generation and completion become brilliantly evident. Thus it profoundly awakened the sage’s unique understanding; ordinary phenomena could not compare with it. Yet Fuxi looked upward to observe and downward to examine: how can we know that the River Chart was not one among the things he observed? Earlier Confucian scholars said that, when the sage composed the Book of Changes, the framework by which he took phenomena as his models must have had a particularly immediate and pertinent basis. Surely they meant the River Chart.

Book of Documents
“Be heedful of Heaven’s mandate; attend to the times and to the first stirrings of change.”
Xu Huan 許瓛

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: The topic is inherently grand and dignified, but writers mostly recycle earlier compositions, making them tiresome to read. This essay is solemn in diction and correct in meaning. It captures the atmosphere of the court of Yu, admonishing and urging on its officials. It deserves praise.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Its diction and tone are gentle and elegant, and its writing vigorous and strong. It expresses almost fully the meaning of preserving good government. It certainly merits recommendation for a high ranking.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: It comes close to portraying the sage ruler’s anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline.

Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: Its explanation of the two words “times” and “first stirrings” does not depart from the original purport.

To show the utmost reverence toward Heaven, one must exercise the utmost caution in oneself, for Heaven’s mandate does not lie outside human affairs. How, then, could anyone wishing to show the utmost reverence toward Heaven’s mandate fail to exercise care concerning the times and the first stirrings of change? title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
歌之意如此謂夫天之有命雖非諄諄然以告
人而命之在天則實凜凜乎其可畏彼其保佑
申錫於人者固宜有以予之矣然予之未幾而
亦或奪之予奪之際天命之所在也靈承于下
者其可不致夫戒勅之意乎寵綏眷顧于人者
固宜有以福之矣然福之未久而亦復禍之禍
福之分天命之所寓也對越于上者其可不盡
夫戒嚴之心乎夫天命無常人所當勅而勅天
之道豈可他求亦曰惟時惟幾自其在我者而
===
慎之耳是故自今日觀之功成治定庶尹允諧
時若可以少暇矣然不知理焉亂所倚也苟頃
刻謹畏之不存則怠荒由之而起必兢兢業業
惟時而謹之使無一時之不戒勅可也禮備樂
和百獸率舞事若可以少適矣然不知安焉危
所伏也苟毫髮幾微之不察則禍患由之而生
必洞洞屬屬惟幾而察之使無一事之不戒嚴
可也夫然則天命庶乎其不替而治功庶可以
無虞矣君臣同心可不以是而為務哉嗟夫古
punctuated:
歌之意如此。謂夫天之有命，雖非諄諄然以告人，而命之在天，則實凜凜乎其可畏。彼其保佑申錫於人者，固宜有以予之矣；然予之未幾，而亦或奪之。予奪之際，天命之所在也。靈承于下者，其可不致夫戒勅之意乎？寵綏眷顧于人者，固宜有以福之矣；然福之未久，而亦復禍之。禍福之分，天命之所寓也。對越于上者，其可不盡夫戒嚴之心乎？夫天命無常，人所當勅，而勅天之道，豈可他求？亦曰惟時惟幾，自其在我者而慎之耳。
是故自今日觀之，功成治定，庶尹允諧，時若可以少暇矣。然不知理焉亂所倚也，苟頃刻謹畏之不存，則怠荒由之而起。必兢兢業業，惟時而謹之，使無一時之不戒勅，可也。禮備樂和，百獸率舞，事若可以少適矣。然不知安焉危所伏也，苟毫髮幾微之不察，則禍患由之而生。必洞洞屬屬，惟幾而察之，使無一事之不戒嚴，可也。夫然，則天命庶乎其不替，而治功庶可以無虞矣。君臣同心，可不以是而為務哉？嗟夫！古
translation_en:
…such was the intent of his song. This means that although Heaven does not communicate its mandate by earnestly instructing people, the mandate residing in Heaven is truly awe-inspiring and to be feared. When Heaven protects people and repeatedly bestows its gifts upon them, it surely has reason to grant them its favor. Yet scarcely has it granted that favor when it may withdraw it. In this granting and withdrawing lies Heaven’s mandate. Can those below who reverently receive it fail to exercise vigilance and caution? When Heaven cherishes people, brings them peace, and regards them with favor, it surely has reason to bless them. Yet before those blessings have lasted long, it may again bring calamity upon them. In the distinction between calamity and blessing resides Heaven’s mandate. Can those who reverently respond to Heaven above fail to give their whole hearts to vigilance and reverence? Heaven’s mandate is inconstant, and people must therefore be watchful. Yet how could the way to be heedful of Heaven be sought elsewhere? It consists simply in attending to the times and to the first stirrings of events, exercising care over what lies within oneself.
Thus, viewed from the present moment, achievements are complete, government is settled, and the many chief officials are truly harmonious: the times seem to allow a little leisure. Yet people fail to recognize that disorder leans upon order. If caution and awe are absent for even a moment, negligence and laxity arise from that absence. One must be tremblingly vigilant, attending carefully to the times, so that not a single moment passes without watchfulness and caution. Ritual is complete, music harmonious, and the hundred beasts all dance: affairs seem to permit a little ease. Yet people fail to recognize that danger lurks within security. If the slightest incipient signs escape scrutiny, calamity and trouble arise from them. One must remain deeply reverent and attentive, examining the first stirrings of events, so that not a single affair is left without vigilance and reverence. Only then may Heaven’s mandate remain undiminished and the achievements of government be free from danger. With ruler and ministers united in purpose, can they fail to make this their task? Ah! In antiquity…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖君賢相不以致治爲難而以保治爲難不
以將順爲敬而以責難爲敬故有虞之治已爲
極功而舜與臯陶方且以時幾爲戒以叢脞爲
規蓋其憂勤惕厲之心未始一息而懈也後世
固有治僅小康而其君臣已晏然自足視此亦
可少愧矣有天下國家者尚念茲哉
志以道寧言以道接
張宜
同考試官訓導林批揭書出題本無立意場中多
失於鑿此作措詞莊重得古人進諫之意高薦無忝
同考試官教諭楊批浮華不騁召公忠愛之意藹
然取冠本房允協輿論
考試官侍講張批起講處拈出道字來便異衆作
考試官學士梁批辭氣雅馴宜在所錄
持志聽言一於理此謹德之要也夫內外貴乎
交脩也志以道寧而言以道接則內外一於理
矣謹德之要豈外是哉召公作旅獒以戒武王
而及此意若曰天下之事皆出於道而道者所
punctuated:
聖君賢相不以致治爲難，而以保治爲難；不以將順爲敬，而以責難爲敬。故有虞之治已爲極功，而舜與臯陶方且以時幾爲戒，以叢脞爲規，蓋其憂勤惕厲之心未始一息而懈也。後世固有治僅小康，而其君臣已晏然自足，視此亦可少愧矣。有天下國家者尚念茲哉！
志以道寧，言以道接。
張宜
同考試官訓導林批：揭書出題，本無立意，場中多失於鑿。此作措詞莊重，得古人進諫之意，高薦無忝。
同考試官教諭楊批：浮華不騁，召公忠愛之意藹然。取冠本房，允協輿論。
考試官侍講張批：起講處拈出道字來，便異衆作。
考試官學士梁批：辭氣雅馴，宜在所錄。
持志聽言，一於理，此謹德之要也。夫內外貴乎交脩也，志以道寧，而言以道接，則內外一於理矣。謹德之要，豈外是哉？召公作《旅獒》以戒武王，而及此意，若曰：天下之事皆出於道，而道者所
translation_en:
…sage rulers and worthy ministers regarded preserving good government as difficult, rather than bringing it about; they regarded calling their ruler to difficult undertakings as true respect, rather than accommodating his wishes. Thus, although government under Youyu had already reached the highest achievement, Shun and Gao Yao still cautioned against lapses at any time and at the first subtle signs of change, and admonished against preoccupation with trifles. Their anxious diligence and vigilant care never slackened for a single breath. In later ages, some governments attained only modest peace, yet their rulers and ministers were already complacently satisfied. Compared with this example, they surely ought to feel some shame. May those who possess the realm or govern states and houses bear this in mind!
“Let your purpose be settled by the Way, and receive words according to the Way.”
Zhang Yi
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: “The topic was selected by opening the book, with no predetermined interpretation in mind. Many candidates erred by forcing the meaning. This composition is gravely and dignifiedly worded and captures the spirit of remonstrance among the ancients. It fully merits a high recommendation.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “It does not indulge in florid display; the Duke of Shao’s loyal affection is abundantly evident. Ranking it first in this examining room accords fully with the general judgment.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: “By bringing out the word ‘Way’ in the opening exposition, it immediately distinguishes itself from the other compositions.”
Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: “Its diction and tone are elegant and refined. It deserves inclusion among the selected works.”
To maintain one’s purpose and listen to words in complete accord with principle: this is the essential means of attending carefully to virtue. Inner and outer cultivation must advance together. If one’s purpose is settled by the Way and words are received according to the Way, then both inner and outer will accord wholly with principle. Could the essentials of attending carefully to virtue lie outside this? The Duke of Shao composed ‘The Hounds of Lü’ to admonish King Wu and touched upon this meaning, as though saying: ‘All affairs under Heaven proceed from the Way, and the Way is that which…’

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
當由之理也人君欲愼其德豈可不惟道是由
乎是故端居靜處之時存乎中而主乎氣者有
志焉志患其易馳也不以道寧之則中心無主
而或至於妄發矣故必涵天理於方寸之間使
欲不得以勝義絕物誘於虛靈之外俾氣不至
於動心一念之往果出於正歟則養之順之而
不容遏一念之往果涉於私歟必戒之抑之而
不敢遂夫然則清明在躬而吾之志可寧矣何
妄發之足慮乎至若臨下御衆之時得乎人而
===
入乎耳者有言焉言患其易惑也非以道接之
則聽德不聰而或至於妄受矣故必度理於敷
奏之間不以逆耳而有所拒揆義於獻納之頃
不以遜志而有所從謀或有裨於政也雖芻蕘
行路之賤吾聽之計或無補於時也雖左右在
位之臣吾置之夫然則權衡不撓而人之言可
接矣何妄受之足憂乎吁志以道寧存乎中而
應乎外者有本也言以道接制乎外而養其中
者有則也謹德之要不外乎此而聖賢相授心
punctuated: 當由之理也。人君欲愼其德，豈可不惟道是由乎？是故端居靜處之時，存乎中而主乎氣者，有志焉。志患其易馳也，不以道寧之，則中心無主，而或至於妄發矣。故必涵天理於方寸之間，使欲不得以勝義；絕物誘於虛靈之外，俾氣不至於動心。一念之往，果出於正歟？則養之、順之，而不容遏；一念之往，果涉於私歟？必戒之、抑之，而不敢遂。夫然則清明在躬，而吾之志可寧矣，何妄發之足慮乎？至若臨下御衆之時，得乎人而入乎耳者，有言焉。言患其易惑也，非以道接之，則聽德不聰，而或至於妄受矣。故必度理於敷奏之間，不以逆耳而有所拒；揆義於獻納之頃，不以遜志而有所從。謀或有裨於政也，雖芻蕘行路之賤，吾聽之；計或無補於時也，雖左右在位之臣，吾置之。夫然則權衡不撓，而人之言可接矣，何妄受之足憂乎？吁！志以道寧，存乎中而應乎外者有本也；言以道接，制乎外而養其中者有則也。謹德之要不外乎此，而聖賢相授心
translation_en:
…the principle that ought to be followed. If a ruler wishes to be watchful over his virtue, how can he fail to follow the Way alone? Thus, when he sits composed in quiet seclusion, what abides within and governs his vital energy is his resolve. The danger with resolve is that it readily runs astray. Unless he steadies it through the Way, his heart will lack a master, and he may act rashly. He must therefore nurture Heaven’s principle within his heart, so that desire cannot overcome righteousness, and exclude the enticements of external things from his lucid, receptive mind, so that his vital energy cannot stir his heart. Does an emerging thought truly spring from what is right? Then he must nourish it and follow it, allowing nothing to obstruct it. Does an emerging thought truly involve selfishness? Then he must guard against it and restrain it, never daring to pursue it. In this way, clarity and illumination reside within him, and his resolve can be steadied. What need is there to fear rash impulses?

When he presides over his subordinates and governs the multitude, what comes from others and enters his ears is their speech. The danger with speech is that it readily misleads. Unless he receives it according to the Way, his capacity for listening will lack discernment, and he may accept words rashly. He must therefore assess the principle in what is reported to him, rejecting nothing merely because it offends his ears; he must weigh the righteousness of advice presented to him, following nothing merely because it accords with his wishes. If a proposal benefits government, I will heed it, even if it comes from humble grass-cutters, wood-gatherers, or people on the road. If a plan offers no remedy for the needs of the time, I will set it aside, even if it comes from ministers at my side holding office. In this way, the balance of judgment remains undistorted, and others’ words can be received properly. What need is there to worry about rash acceptance?

Ah! When resolve is steadied through the Way, that which abides within and responds to what is outside has a foundation. When speech is received according to the Way, that which regulates what comes from outside and nourishes what is within has a standard. The essentials of watchfulness over virtue go no further than this, and the heart-mind transmitted from sage to sage and worthy to worthy…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
亦於此而可見矣抑考西旅獻獒之時武王
大業已定獒之受否無大害也而召公惓惓作
書以戒者豈故為是過慮耶蓋創業之君後嗣
取法厲階固不可以生也况四夷聞之從風而
靡則其患不可勝言矣噫以此為防其後猶有
求白狼白鹿如穆王者召公之言誠萬世人君
之龜鑑也哉
詩
王命南仲往城于方出車彭彭旂旐央央
===
天子命我城彼朔方赫赫南仲玁狁于
襄
李錫
同考試官教諭任批南仲旣傳命令眾故軍士皆
知所以出師之意此本章正意也是作能發揮之可取可取
同考試官教諭楊批以王命南仲二句為傳命以
令軍眾最合傳意故錄之以破群疑
同考試官教諭明批說出南仲傳命令眾意其文
法森嚴真知禦戎之策者
punctuated:
亦於此而可見矣。抑考西旅獻獒之時，武王大業已定，獒之受否無大害也，而召公惓惓作書以戒者，豈故為是過慮耶？蓋創業之君，後嗣取法，厲階固不可以生也。况四夷聞之，從風而靡，則其患不可勝言矣。噫！以此為防，其後猶有求白狼白鹿如穆王者，召公之言誠萬世人君之龜鑑也哉！

詩
王命南仲，往城于方。出車彭彭，旂旐央央。天子命我，城彼朔方。赫赫南仲，玁狁于襄。

李錫

同考試官教諭任批：南仲旣傳命令眾，故軍士皆知所以出師之意，此本章正意也。是作能發揮之，可取，可取！

同考試官教諭楊批：以「王命南仲」二句為傳命以令軍眾，最合傳意，故錄之以破群疑。

同考試官教諭明批：說出南仲傳命令眾意，其文法森嚴，真知禦戎之策者。
translation_en:
…can likewise be seen here. Now consider the time when Xilü presented a mastiff: King Wu’s great enterprise was already secured, and accepting or refusing the mastiff would have done no great harm. Yet the Duke of Shao earnestly composed a document to admonish him. Was he deliberately indulging in excessive anxiety? The ruler who establishes a dynasty becomes a model for his descendants; a source of calamity must therefore never be allowed to arise. Moreover, if the peoples of the four quarters heard of this and bent to follow his example like grass before the wind, the resulting troubles would be beyond description. Alas! Even with this warning as a safeguard, later there were still rulers like King Mu, who sought white wolves and white deer. The Duke of Shao’s words are truly a mirror for rulers in all ages!

Book of Odes
“The king commanded Nanzhong to go and build fortifications at Fang. The chariots went forth in multitudes; the banners streamed in profusion. The Son of Heaven commanded us to fortify that northern region. Illustrious was Nanzhong: the Xianyun were swept away.”

Li Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, School Instructor: Since Nanzhong had transmitted the command to give orders to the troops, all the soldiers understood the purpose of the expedition. This is the proper meaning of the stanza. This composition succeeds in developing it. Worthy of selection, worthy of selection!

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor: Taking the two lines beginning “The king commanded Nanzhong” as the transmission of the royal command to give orders to the troops accords most closely with the commentary’s meaning. I have therefore selected this composition to dispel the various doubts.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ming, School Instructor: It brings out the meaning of Nanzhong’s transmitting the command to give orders to the troops. Its composition is rigorously ordered. Here is someone who truly understands the strategy for defending against the Rong.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍講張批讀此可以想見西周命將出師之盛
考試官學士梁批通篇明贍可觀
大將之傳命以令眾也軍容盛而士志齊威名
著而遠夷服蓋用師之道惟以直而為壯耳大
將之所以盛軍容而齊士志著威名而服遠夷
者其皆從傳命令眾中來耶周王於其還而述
此以勞之宜矣昔南仲當獫狁匪茹之時膺長
子率師之任想其傳命令眾之意謂夫獫狁之
難未平則邊鄙之民不息天討固不容以不加
===
也明明天子則命我南仲往朔方而城守之焉
蓋惟以守備為本而不以攻戰為先也汝三軍
之士其亦知所以敵王之愾者乎邊鄙之民不
息則中國之害未除王師固不容以不動也有
嚴天子則命我南仲城朔方以備禦之焉蓋先
為不可勝以待敵之可勝也汝貔貅之士其亦
知所以分主之憂者乎斯時也大將之號令一
施三軍之精采百倍我出我車則彭彭而眾盛
建彼旐旟則央央而鮮明王命往城之意不獨
punctuated:
考試官侍講張批：讀此，可以想見西周命將出師之盛。
考試官學士梁批：通篇明贍可觀。
大將之傳命以令眾也，軍容盛而士志齊，威名著而遠夷服。蓋用師之道，惟以直而為壯耳。大將之所以盛軍容而齊士志、著威名而服遠夷者，其皆從傳命令眾中來耶？周王於其還而述此以勞之，宜矣。昔南仲當獫狁匪茹之時，膺長子率師之任，想其傳命令眾之意，謂夫獫狁之難未平，則邊鄙之民不息，天討固不容以不加也。明明天子，則命我南仲往朔方而城守之焉。蓋惟以守備為本，而不以攻戰為先也。汝三軍之士，其亦知所以敵王之愾者乎？邊鄙之民不息，則中國之害未除，王師固不容以不動也。有嚴天子，則命我南仲城朔方以備禦之焉。蓋先為不可勝，以待敵之可勝也。汝貔貅之士，其亦知所以分主之憂者乎？斯時也，大將之號令一施，三軍之精采百倍。我出我車，則彭彭而眾盛；建彼旐旟，則央央而鮮明。王命往城之意，不獨
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: Reading this, one can picture the grandeur with which the Western Zhou appointed commanders and dispatched armies.
Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: Clear and ample throughout; worthy of appreciation.
