之本意，然豈無一言之可取者哉？取其所可取者，以附於綱目凡例之下，以相羽翼，是亦吾後人讀朱子之書、體朱子之心者之公義也。奚必如公羊墨守者之所爲哉？欽惟皇上緝熙聖學，日就光明，行將以通鑑綱目之書同尚書經傳進講于經筵之上。在執事則持此以往耳，生何人，敢與聞乎此？惟進而教之，幸甚。
第三問
張愈
同考試官教諭林批：此策備道禮樂之情文，有關世道之隆替。末復昭頌聖德，屬意有司，以端治化之本，是豈徒泛泛稱述者比邪？因事納忠，子亦有見矣。
考試官侍講張批：檃栝前代禮樂之凡，推本聖祖功德之盛，其亦通達治體者，薦何忝？
考試官學士梁批：周詳曲折，忠義藹然。讀之終篇，尚覺意
translation_en:
…the original intent, yet could there not be even a single statement worth adopting? To take what is worth adopting and append it beneath the General Principles of the Outline and Details, so that they support one another, is also the impartial duty of us later readers who study Master Zhu’s writings and enter into his spirit. Why must we behave like those who stubbornly defend the Gongyang tradition?
With reverence I reflect that His Majesty continually advances and illuminates his sagely learning, daily attaining greater brilliance. Soon the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian gangmu) will be expounded at the Classics Colloquium alongside the Book of Documents and its commentaries. You, sir, need only carry this understanding forward. Who am I, a mere student, to presume to have a part in this? I would be most fortunate if you would further instruct me.
Third Policy Question
Zhang Yu
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: This policy essay fully explains the inner substance and outward forms of rites and music, which bear upon the flourishing and decline of the moral order. At its close it again openly praises the imperial virtue and directs its hopes toward the responsible officials, so as to set right the foundations of governance and moral transformation. How could this be compared with mere commonplace praise? You offer loyal counsel in response to the matter at hand; you too have discernment.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: It summarizes the essentials of rites and music in earlier ages and traces them back to the abundance of the Sagely Ancestor’s achievements and virtue. Its author, too, understands the principles of governance. What shame could there be in recommending him?
Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: Thorough and attentive to every intricacy, it overflows with loyalty and righteousness. Having read the entire essay, I still feel that its meaning…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
在言外他日居言路論事時惟更加剴切可也勉旃勉旃
先王禮樂之治其見於班歐二子之書者
詳矣是皆先正格言而二子述之今自其
說而觀之則執事之所謂三王禮樂之原
與後代禮樂不興之故皆可以槩見而所
謂我
朝禮樂刑政四達不悖之實亦可以卽此而
仰窺萬一矣請竝舉其畧以復于執事昔
聖人象天地而制禮樂所以通神明立人
===
倫正性情節萬事者也樂以治內而為同
禮以修外而為異同則和親而不怨異則
畏敬而不爭著之於享獻辭受登降跪拜
之間發之於詩歌詠言鐘石筦弦之際蓋
嘉其敬意而不及於財賄美其歡心而不
流其聲音此禮樂之本也民心以是而節
民聲以是而和而又政以行之刑以防之
則禮樂刑政四達而不悖矣此非班固氏
禮樂為急之說乎矧先王禮樂之器若車
punctuated:
在言外。他日居言路論事時，惟更加剴切可也。勉旃，勉旃！

先王禮樂之治，其見於班歐二子之書者詳矣。是皆先正格言，而二子述之。今自其說而觀之，則執事之所謂三王禮樂之原與後代禮樂不興之故，皆可以槩見；而所謂我朝禮樂刑政四達不悖之實，亦可以卽此而仰窺萬一矣。請竝舉其畧，以復于執事。昔聖人象天地而制禮樂，所以通神明、立人倫、正性情、節萬事者也。樂以治內而為同，禮以修外而為異。同則和親而不怨，異則畏敬而不爭。著之於享獻辭受登降跪拜之間，發之於詩歌詠言鐘石筦弦之際。蓋嘉其敬意而不及於財賄，美其歡心而不流其聲音，此禮樂之本也。民心以是而節，民聲以是而和，而又政以行之，刑以防之，則禮樂刑政四達而不悖矣。此非班固氏禮樂為急之說乎？矧先王禮樂之器，若車
translation_en:
…lies beyond the words. When in future you occupy a remonstrance post and discuss affairs, you need only make your arguments still more incisive and pertinent. Strive on, strive on!

The former kings’ governance through rites and music is recorded in detail in the writings of Ban and Ou. These are all authoritative sayings of earlier worthies, transmitted by those two writers. Examining their accounts, we can gain a general understanding both of what you call the origins of the Three Kings’ rites and music and of the reasons why rites and music failed to flourish in later ages. From these accounts we may also respectfully glimpse a tiny part of the reality of our dynasty’s rites, music, punishments, and administration operating everywhere without conflict. Allow me to outline these matters together in reply to you.

In antiquity, the sages modeled rites and music on Heaven and Earth, using them to communicate with spiritual powers, establish human relationships, rectify people’s nature and feelings, and regulate all affairs. Music orders the inner life and brings people together; rites cultivate outward conduct and distinguish people’s respective positions. Unity brings harmony and affection without resentment; distinction brings awe and respect without contention. These find expression in offerings and presentations, declining and accepting, ascending and descending, kneeling and bowing; they issue forth in poetry, song, chanted words, bells, stone chimes, pipes, and strings. What is prized is the reverent intention, without extending that valuation to material gifts; what is admired is the joyful heart, without allowing its sounds to become unrestrained. This is the foundation of rites and music. Through these, the people’s hearts are regulated and their voices harmonized. When administration further puts them into practice and punishments guard against violations, rites, music, punishments, and administration operate everywhere without conflict. Is this not Ban Gu’s argument that rites and music are a matter of urgent importance? Moreover, the implements of the former kings’ rites and music, such as carriages…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
與冕弁尊爵俎豆金石絲竹之屬皆其日
用朝夕之所以教民從事者蓋不出于居
處動作衣服飲食之間而自足以爲孝慈
友悌忠信仁義之行天下皆安習而行之
不知所以遷善遠罪而成俗也後之有天
下者則不然朝夕從事於簿書獄訟兵食
間曰此所以爲政而治民也至於三代禮
樂但具其名物而藏於有司時出而用之
於郊廟朝廷中曰此爲禮而教民也當時
===
士大夫尚且習其器而不知其意忘其本
而存其末而況於天下之人安能諭禮樂
之意被教化以成俗乎是其治出於二而
禮樂爲虚文矣此非歐陽氏禮樂達於天
下之說乎噫卽班固氏之說觀之則三代
禮樂之原其可知矣卽歐陽氏之說觀之
則後世禮樂不興之故其可知矣執事慨
然念此而復以仲尼季札之事引而伸之
愚於此重有感焉何則禮由陰作樂由陽
punctuated:
與冕弁、尊爵、俎豆、金石絲竹之屬，皆其日用朝夕之所以教民從事者。蓋不出于居處動作、衣服飲食之間，而自足以爲孝慈友悌、忠信仁義之行。天下皆安習而行之，不知所以遷善遠罪而成俗也。後之有天下者則不然，朝夕從事於簿書獄訟兵食間，曰：「此所以爲政而治民也。」至於三代禮樂，但具其名物而藏於有司，時出而用之於郊廟朝廷中，曰：「此爲禮而教民也。」當時士大夫尚且習其器而不知其意，忘其本而存其末，而況於天下之人，安能諭禮樂之意，被教化以成俗乎？是其治出於二，而禮樂爲虚文矣。此非歐陽氏禮樂達於天下之說乎？
噫！卽班固氏之說觀之，則三代禮樂之原其可知矣；卽歐陽氏之說觀之，則後世禮樂不興之故其可知矣。執事慨然念此，而復以仲尼季札之事引而伸之，愚於此重有感焉。何則？禮由陰作，樂由陽
translation_en:
…and ceremonial crowns and caps, wine vessels and cups, offering stands and dishes, bells and chime stones, stringed instruments and bamboo pipes—all were things used daily, morning and evening, through which the former kings taught the people how to conduct themselves. These did not extend beyond dwelling and movement, clothing and food, yet they sufficed to bring about conduct marked by filial devotion and parental kindness, brotherly affection and respect, loyalty and trustworthiness, benevolence and righteousness. All under Heaven grew accustomed to these practices and followed them at ease, unaware of how they were moving toward goodness, distancing themselves from wrongdoing, and establishing good customs. Those who later possessed all under Heaven did otherwise. Morning and evening they occupied themselves with registers and documents, judicial cases and litigation, military affairs and provisions, saying, “These are the means by which we conduct government and rule the people.” As for the rites and music of the Three Dynasties, they merely provided the prescribed objects and stored them with the responsible offices, bringing them out occasionally for use at the suburban sacrifices, ancestral temples, and court, saying, “These constitute the rites by which we teach the people.” Even the scholar-officials of those times were familiar with the implements but did not understand their meaning; they forgot the foundations while preserving the outward details. How much less could the people throughout the realm understand the meaning of rites and music and receive their transforming instruction so as to establish good customs? Thus their government proceeded along two separate tracks, and rites and music became empty forms. Is this not Master Ouyang’s argument concerning the extension of rites and music throughout the realm?
Alas! Viewed through Ban Gu’s argument, the origins of the rites and music of the Three Dynasties can be understood; viewed through Master Ouyang’s argument, the reasons why rites and music failed to flourish in later ages can be understood. You, honored examiner, have reflected deeply and with concern upon this, and have further developed the argument by invoking the affairs of Zhongni and Ji Zha. On this point I, in my ignorance, am moved once more. Why is this? Rites arise from yin, and music from yang…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
来禮者理也樂者和也陰陽之序必先理
而後和是禮先而樂後矣然禮之與樂俱
有情有文如聲氣性情者樂之情也節文
度數者禮之文也知禮樂之情者能作識
禮樂之文者能述知禮樂之情者固尤有
難於識禮樂之文者矣非禮樂自有彼此
難易之分也雖然仲尼大聖也於禮樂之
情其知之矣彼季札雖賢亦不過能識其
文耳然而季札聘魯之時能備知夫韶夏
===
大武之樂豈仲尼於二代之禮乃不能徵
之於杞宋之邦耶蓋季札之所識者亦識
其文而已使杞宋而足徵固足以徵仲尼
之言使仲尼而得位則且將制禮作樂以
比隆于前世豈獨識禮樂之文而已哉愚
於此故重有感焉嗟夫三代以前一宇宙
也自秦以下又一宇宙也惟仲尼不得位
故三王禮樂之原不復行於天下後世遂
使秦之餘毒餘千載而不能救雖以漢唐
punctuated:
来。禮者，理也；樂者，和也。陰陽之序，必先理而後和，是禮先而樂後矣。然禮之與樂，俱有情有文。如聲氣性情者，樂之情也；節文度數者，禮之文也。知禮樂之情者能作，識禮樂之文者能述。知禮樂之情者，固尤有難於識禮樂之文者矣，非禮樂自有彼此難易之分也。雖然，仲尼大聖也，於禮樂之情，其知之矣。彼季札雖賢，亦不過能識其文耳。然而季札聘魯之時，能備知夫韶、夏、大武之樂，豈仲尼於二代之禮，乃不能徵之於杞宋之邦耶？蓋季札之所識者，亦識其文而已。使杞宋而足徵，固足以徵仲尼之言；使仲尼而得位，則且將制禮作樂，以比隆于前世，豈獨識禮樂之文而已哉？愚於此故重有感焉。
嗟夫！三代以前，一宇宙也；自秦以下，又一宇宙也。惟仲尼不得位，故三王禮樂之原不復行於天下。後世遂使秦之餘毒餘千載而不能救，雖以漢唐
translation_en:
…comes forth. Ritual is order; music is harmony. In the sequence of yin and yang, order must precede harmony: thus ritual comes first and music follows. Yet ritual and music both possess an inner substance and an outward form. Sound, vital breath, human nature, and feelings constitute the inner substance of music; articulated patterns, measures, and numerical prescriptions constitute the outward form of ritual. Those who understand the inner substance of ritual and music can create them; those who recognize their outward forms can transmit them. Understanding their inner substance is indeed harder than recognizing their outward forms. It is not that ritual and music themselves differ in difficulty.
Nevertheless, Zhongni [Confucius] was a great sage and understood the inner substance of ritual and music. Worthy though Ji Zha was, he could do no more than recognize their outward forms. Yet when Ji Zha visited Lu as an envoy, he could identify fully the music of Shao, Xia, and Dawu. Could Zhongni really have been unable to find evidence for the rituals of the two dynasties [Xia and Shang] in the states of Qi and Song? What Ji Zha recognized was, after all, merely their outward form. Had Qi and Song furnished sufficient evidence, it would certainly have corroborated Zhongni’s words. Had Zhongni attained a position of authority, he would have instituted rituals and composed music to rival the splendor of earlier ages. How could he merely have recognized their outward forms? This is why I am once again deeply moved by this matter.
Alas! The Three Dynasties and the ages before them constituted one world; from Qin onward there was another. Because Zhongni did not attain a position of authority, the foundational principles of the ritual and music of the Three Kings were never again put into practice throughout the realm. Later ages consequently allowed Qin’s lingering poison to persist for more than a thousand years without remedy. Even with the Han and Tang…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
宋之英君誼辟曾有志於致治者尚不能
有所持循依據以為作禮樂之本可勝嘆
哉天生聖人應時而作是必有待於今日
者矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝德肩堯禹功邁商周治定而制禮
功成而作樂凡冠昏喪祭飲射讀法居室
器用之禮自漢唐以來不能達之于天下
者今則大禮與天地同其節凡
郊廟社稷山川百神朝會燕享之樂自漢唐以
===
來不能傳之於來裔者今則大樂與天地
同其和
聖子神孫
本支百世守而勿失頌聲作焉方今
聖明在上敬
天法
祖致治保邦存側身修行之誠行勤恤民隱之
政如執事之所謂申明舊制禁士民奢僭
之弊庶幾所以為節用裕民之一助者亦
punctuated:
宋之英君誼辟，曾有志於致治者，尚不能有所持循依據，以為作禮樂之本，可勝嘆哉！天生聖人，應時而作，是必有待於今日者矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，德肩堯禹，功邁商周。治定而制禮，功成而作樂。凡冠昏喪祭、飲射讀法、居室器用之禮，自漢唐以來不能達之于天下者，今則大禮與天地同其節；凡郊廟社稷、山川百神、朝會燕享之樂，自漢唐以來不能傳之於來裔者，今則大樂與天地同其和。聖子神孫，本支百世，守而勿失，頌聲作焉。
方今聖明在上，敬天法祖，致治保邦，存側身修行之誠，行勤恤民隱之政。如執事之所謂申明舊制，禁士民奢僭之弊，庶幾所以為節用裕民之一助者，亦
translation_en:
…and Song, even those outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns who aspired to good government still had nothing to follow or rely upon as a foundation for establishing rites and music. How deeply lamentable! Heaven brings forth sages to arise when their time comes; surely this fulfillment had to await the present day.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao equaled Yao and Yu in virtue and surpassed the Shang and Zhou in achievement. Once order was established, he instituted rites; once his achievements were complete, he created music. All the rites governing capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, communal drinking, archery, reading the laws, dwellings, and utensils—which, since the Han and Tang, had not been extended throughout the realm—now constitute great ritual whose measured order accords with Heaven and Earth. All the music for the suburban and ancestral temple sacrifices, the altars of Soil and Grain, the mountains and rivers and the hundred spirits, court assemblies, and banquets—which, since the Han and Tang, had not been transmitted to later generations—now constitutes great music whose harmony accords with Heaven and Earth. His sagely sons and divine grandsons, the main line and collateral branches for a hundred generations, preserve these without loss, and songs of praise arise.
Now our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above, revering Heaven and following his ancestors, bringing good government and securing the realm. He sincerely humbles himself and cultivates his conduct, and implements policies that diligently attend to the people's hidden hardships. As you, honored examiners, have said, reaffirming the established regulations and prohibiting extravagance and the usurpation of status privileges among scholars and commoners may provide some assistance in economizing expenditure and enriching the people; this also…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
誠首務也然獨不曰民不從所令而從所
好乎儻自今以始凡左右常伯綴衣虎賁
之屬俱能上體
聖心率先儉朴動以封靡爲不祥之物更相戒
飭以漸成美化則自閭閻市井至敷天之
下其殆有不令而從焉者矣禮樂刑政四
達不悖之實庶其在此未知執事以爲然
否
第四問
趙祐
同考試官訓導趙批道學一策本未易知是荅於程
朱師友源淵處歷歷有據而文亦精到其學知好古者歟高薦何忝
同考試官教諭周批辨析程朱事實詳悉似非口
耳之學可到意嘗究心於是者歟
考試官侍講張批先賢授受之詳此子悉能叙述亦可見
其篤信好學矣
考試官學士梁批程朱之書如水由地中行讀其書不知其
師友淵源可乎此對強記不遺亦塲屋中難得之士也
punctuated:
誠首務也。然獨不曰：「民不從所令，而從所好」乎？儻自今以始，凡左右常伯、綴衣、虎賁之屬，俱能上體聖心，率先儉朴，動以封靡爲不祥之物，更相戒飭，以漸成美化，則自閭閻市井至敷天之下，其殆有不令而從焉者矣。禮樂刑政四達不悖之實，庶其在此。未知執事以爲然否？

第四問
趙祐

同考試官訓導趙批：「道學一策，本未易知。是荅於程朱師友源淵處，歷歷有據，而文亦精到。其學知好古者歟？高薦何忝！」

同考試官教諭周批：「辨析程朱事實詳悉，似非口耳之學可到。意嘗究心於是者歟？」

考試官侍講張批：「先賢授受之詳，此子悉能叙述，亦可見其篤信好學矣。」

考試官學士梁批：「程朱之書，如水由地中行。讀其書，不知其師友淵源，可乎？此對強記不遺，亦塲屋中難得之士也。」
translation_en:
…is indeed a foremost priority. Yet is it not said, “The people follow not what they are commanded to do, but what their superiors favor”? If, from this time onward, all the senior attendants, wardrobe officials, and imperial guards at the sovereign’s side could embody the imperial intentions, take the lead in frugality and simplicity, consistently regard extravagance [?] as something inauspicious, and admonish one another, they would gradually bring about an admirable moral transformation. Then, from the lanes and marketplaces to all under Heaven, there would surely be people who followed without being commanded. Here, perhaps, lies the practical realization of ritual, music, punishments, and government operating everywhere without conflict. I do not know whether you, sir, consider this correct.

Fourth Question
Zhao You

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Assistant Instructor: “This policy question on the Learning of the Way is by its nature difficult to comprehend. In discussing the origins of the Cheng brothers’ and Zhu Xi’s learning among their teachers and friends, this answer supplies clear evidence at every point; its writing is also refined and exact. Is he one who acquires knowledge through study and loves antiquity? He fully deserves a high recommendation!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “His analysis of the facts concerning the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi is detailed and thorough. This seems beyond the reach of learning that merely passes from ear to mouth. I imagine he has devoted serious thought to this subject.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: “This candidate can recount in full the details of how the former worthies transmitted and received their learning. This also reveals his steadfast faith and love of learning.”

Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: “The writings of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi are like water flowing through the earth. Can one read their writings without knowing the origins of their learning among teachers and friends? This response displays a powerful memory that omits nothing. He, too, is a scholar rarely encountered in the examination halls.”

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
水之流也必窮其源會其派而後水之全
體可知木之植也必探其本視其末而後
木之大用可試道學之在人猶水之有源
流木之有本末也苟不自其師友門人之
學而求之又何以得其授受之詳與其所
學之要哉蓋嘗求之二程夫子與子朱子
之學矣有宋之興也五星聚奎文風振起
而程子出焉紫氣入斗文教大興而朱子
出焉程子倡正學於千載不傳之後朱子
===
集大成於諸儒異同之間皆能使斯道粲
然復明於世故五峯胡氏謂二程之功可
比孔子之作春秋孟子之闢楊墨而鶴山
魏氏謂孟子之功不在禹下朱子之功不
在孟子下由是觀之其爲大有功於聖門
則一也然論其所以學則程子以誠敬爲
入門以踐履爲實地自致知以至於知止
自灑掃應對而至於窮理盡性朱子則主
敬以立其本窮理以致其知反躬以踐其
punctuated: 水之流也，必窮其源，會其派，而後水之全體可知；木之植也，必探其本，視其末，而後木之大用可試。道學之在人，猶水之有源流、木之有本末也。苟不自其師友門人之學而求之，又何以得其授受之詳與其所學之要哉？蓋嘗求之二程夫子與子朱子之學矣。有宋之興也，五星聚奎，文風振起，而程子出焉；紫氣入斗，文教大興，而朱子出焉。程子倡正學於千載不傳之後，朱子集大成於諸儒異同之間，皆能使斯道粲然復明於世。故五峯胡氏謂二程之功可比孔子之作《春秋》、孟子之闢楊墨，而鶴山魏氏謂孟子之功不在禹下，朱子之功不在孟子下。由是觀之，其爲大有功於聖門則一也。然論其所以學，則程子以誠敬爲入門，以踐履爲實地，自致知以至於知止，自灑掃應對而至於窮理盡性；朱子則主敬以立其本，窮理以致其知，反躬以踐其
translation_en:
To understand flowing water, one must trace its source to the utmost and bring its branches together; only then can water be known in its entirety. To understand a growing tree, one must investigate its roots and examine its branch tips; only then can its full usefulness be put to the test. The Learning of the Way among human beings is like water with its source and streams, or a tree with its roots and branches. Unless one seeks it through the learning of its teachers, friends, and disciples, how can one grasp the particulars of its transmission and the essentials of what they studied? I have sought these in the learning of the two Masters Cheng and Master Zhu.

At the rise of the Song dynasty, the five planets gathered in the constellation Kui, literary culture flourished, and the Masters Cheng emerged. Purple vapor entered the constellation Dou, cultural instruction flourished greatly, and Master Zhu emerged. The Masters Cheng championed orthodox learning after its transmission had lapsed for a thousand years; Master Zhu brought it to full fruition amid the agreements and disagreements of the various scholars. All enabled this Way to shine forth brilliantly in the world once again. Thus Hu Wufeng said that the achievement of the two Chengs could be compared to Kongzi’s composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals and Mengzi’s refutation of Yang Zhu and Mo Di. Wei Heshan said that Mengzi’s achievement was no less than Yu’s, and Master Zhu’s no less than Mengzi’s. Viewed in this light, they were alike in rendering great service to the tradition of the sages.

Yet, when discussing their approaches to learning, the Masters Cheng took sincerity and reverent attentiveness as the gateway and practical conduct as the firm ground. They proceeded from extending knowledge to knowing where to rest, and from sweeping and cleaning and responding to others to investigating principle exhaustively and fully realizing human nature. Master Zhu, for his part, made reverent attentiveness central in order to establish the foundation, investigated principle exhaustively in order to extend knowledge, and examined himself in order to put into practice its …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
實而敬又貫通乎三者之間成始而成終
焉是其為學之要則一也夫程子之學雖
曰反求之六經而後得然其入德造道之
始實本於濂溪故其自言曰昔受學於周
茂叔每令尋仲尼顏子樂處所樂何事此
其授受之正非若范文正之於張橫渠粗
發其端而已也朱子之學雖曰博求經傳
徧交當世有識之士然其始終造就之功
實賴於延平故其稱述延平之語一則曰
===
愚聞之師二則曰愚聞之師此其承受之
大非若胡籍溪劉屏山但稟學於初年而
已也程子之與張橫渠邵堯夫從游為最
久論者謂橫渠以禮為教堯夫以數為竒
似乎不同道矣殊不知此蓋各舉其盛而
言耳若論其要歸則子厚之禮未始不主
於敬而敬所以為禮之本也康節之數未
始不根於理而理所以該乎數之用也三
子之道果相牴牾乎朱子與張南軒吕伯
punctuated:
實，而敬又貫通乎三者之間，成始而成終焉。是其為學之要則一也。
夫程子之學，雖曰反求之六經而後得，然其入德造道之始，實本於濂溪。故其自言曰：「昔受學於周茂叔，每令尋仲尼顏子樂處，所樂何事。」此其授受之正，非若范文正之於張橫渠，粗發其端而已也。朱子之學，雖曰博求經傳，徧交當世有識之士，然其始終造就之功，實賴於延平。故其稱述延平之語，一則曰：「愚聞之師。」二則曰：「愚聞之師。」此其承受之大，非若胡籍溪、劉屏山，但稟學於初年而已也。
程子之與張橫渠、邵堯夫，從游為最久。論者謂橫渠以禮為教，堯夫以數為竒，似乎不同道矣。殊不知此蓋各舉其盛而言耳。若論其要歸，則子厚之禮，未始不主於敬，而敬所以為禮之本也；康節之數，未始不根於理，而理所以該乎數之用也。三子之道，果相牴牾乎？朱子與張南軒、吕伯
translation_en:
…its practical substance; reverent attentiveness, moreover, runs through all three, bringing them to completion from beginning to end. Thus the essentials of their learning are one and the same.
Although Master Cheng is said to have attained his learning by turning back to seek it in the Six Classics, his first steps in advancing in virtue and attaining the Way were actually grounded in the teaching of Lianxi. Thus he himself said: “Formerly, when I studied under Zhou Maoshu, he always bade me seek where Zhongni and Yanzi found their joy, and what it was that they delighted in.” Such was the authentic transmission of teaching he received. It was not merely the broad indication of a starting point that Fan Wenzheng gave Zhang Hengqu. Although Master Zhu is said to have sought widely through the classics and their commentaries and associated extensively with knowledgeable men of his age, his formation from beginning to end actually depended upon Yanping. Thus, when recounting Yanping’s words, he says in one instance, “I, in my ignorance, heard this from my teacher,” and in another, “I, in my ignorance, heard this from my teacher.” Such was the magnitude of the teaching he inherited. It was not like his learning from Hu Jixi and Liu Pingshan, from whom he received instruction only in his early years.
Master Cheng’s association with Zhang Hengqu and Shao Yaofu was the longest. Commentators say that Hengqu taught through ritual, while Yaofu distinguished himself through numbers, making it appear that they followed different Ways. They fail to recognize that these statements merely single out what was most prominent in each man’s learning. If we consider their essential purport, Zihou’s [Zhang Hengqu’s] ritual was always centered upon reverent attentiveness, and reverent attentiveness provides the foundation of ritual; Kangjie’s [Shao Yaofu’s] numbers were always rooted in principle, and principle encompasses the workings of numbers. Did the Ways of these three masters truly contradict one another? Master Zhu, together with Zhang Nanxuan and Lü Bo…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
恭講學為最密說者謂南軒之論仁多不
合伯恭之論史記多失正似乎不同志矣
殊不知此特一時之事耳若論其大本則
敬夫辨義利於毫釐之間乃後世學者之
大防也成公闡河洛微言之旨乃中原文
獻之正脉也三子之學果相背馳乎程子
之門人若楊中立之天資穎悟游定夫之
德宇溫粹謝良佐之英果明決强力不倦
吕與叔之脩身好學深潜縝密皆高第也
===
而卒傳其道者龜山一人而已故豫章延
平之學有所本而傳之無弊焉朱子之門
人若黃直卿之造詣純篤廖德明之學有
根據蔡季通之精識博聞推明易學蔡仲
黙之潜心書範闡發幽微皆高第也而深
得其傳者勉齋一人而已故考亭行狀之
作非他人之所能預焉此其師友相傳之
槩門人承繼之凡載於史冊者班班可考
若其道學之淵微心法之蘊奧固非愚生
punctuated: 恭講學為最密。說者謂南軒之論仁多不合，伯恭之論史記多失正，似乎不同志矣。殊不知此特一時之事耳。若論其大本，則敬夫辨義利於毫釐之間，乃後世學者之大防也；成公闡河洛微言之旨，乃中原文獻之正脉也。三子之學果相背馳乎？程子之門人，若楊中立之天資穎悟，游定夫之德宇溫粹，謝良佐之英果明決、强力不倦，吕與叔之脩身好學、深潜縝密，皆高第也。而卒傳其道者，龜山一人而已。故豫章、延平之學有所本，而傳之無弊焉。朱子之門人，若黃直卿之造詣純篤，廖德明之學有根據，蔡季通之精識博聞、推明易學，蔡仲黙之潜心書範、闡發幽微，皆高第也。而深得其傳者，勉齋一人而已。故考亭行狀之作，非他人之所能預焉。此其師友相傳之槩、門人承繼之凡，載於史冊者，班班可考。若其道學之淵微、心法之蘊奧，固非愚生
translation_en:
…gong were his closest companions in discussing learning. Some commentators say that Nanxuan’s discussions of benevolence often diverged from his, and that Bogong’s discussions of historical records often departed from correctness, so that they seem not to have shared the same aspirations. They fail to realize that these were merely matters of a particular time. As for their fundamental principles, Jingfu’s discrimination between righteousness and profit, down to the finest distinctions, provided a great safeguard for later scholars; Chenggong’s elucidation of the subtle teachings of the He-Luo masters represented the orthodox transmission of the Central Plain’s cultural learning. Did the learning of these three masters really run counter to one another?

Among Master Cheng’s disciples, Yang Zhongli, with his innate intelligence and understanding; You Dingfu, with his warm and pure moral bearing; Xie Liangzuo, with his outstanding resolve, clear judgment, and tireless exertion; and Lü Yushu, with his self-cultivation, love of learning, profound reflection, and meticulous care, were all distinguished pupils. Yet in the end, Guishan alone transmitted his Way. Thus the learning of Yuzhang and Yanping had a foundation, and its transmission was free from distortion.

Among Master Zhu’s disciples, Huang Zhiqing, whose attainments were pure and steadfast; Liao Deming, whose learning had firm foundations; Cai Jitong, whose penetrating understanding and extensive knowledge advanced and clarified the study of the Changes; and Cai Zhongmo, who devoted himself to the Documents and its Great Plan, elucidating their hidden subtleties, were all distinguished pupils. Yet Mianzhai alone profoundly grasped what his master transmitted. Thus the composition of the account of Kaoting’s life and conduct was a task in which no one else could have taken part.

These are the broad outlines of transmission among teachers and friends, and of succession among disciples. Recorded in the histories, they can be clearly verified. As for the profound subtleties of their learning of the Way and the hidden depths of their methods of cultivating the mind, these are certainly beyond what an ignorant student such as I…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
末學之所能盡也雖然程朱之教雖同而
程子之門人或有流於禪學者何哉蓋由
其材識英敏往往過於高遠而朱子亦謂
其只見上一截道理而少下面著實工夫
故其末流之弊如此也孔門傳道之任惟
曾子以魯得之良有以夫管見區區未知
是否惟執事教之幸甚
第五問
李錫
===
同考試官教諭任批書學之問場中多不能對是
策明達殆盡而文氣不凡可羨可羨
同考試官教諭楊批說字書作於古變於後至我
朝而歸於正明白詳悉是用錄出
同考試官教諭胡批書學切於日用而學者漫不之
省此篇自源徂委考究精詳亦博雅之士也
考試官侍講張批通篇文有氣槩不獨取其記憶而已
考試官學士梁批字書源委考論精切他卷罕及也
考書學之繁而嗟後世之變古考字體之
punctuated:
末學之所能盡也。雖然，程朱之教雖同，而程子之門人或有流於禪學者，何哉？蓋由其材識英敏，往往過於高遠，而朱子亦謂其只見上一截道理，而少下面著實工夫，故其末流之弊如此也。孔門傳道之任，惟曾子以魯得之，良有以夫！管見區區，未知是否，惟執事教之，幸甚。

第五問
李錫

同考試官教諭任批：書學之問，場中多不能對，是策明達殆盡，而文氣不凡，可羨可羨！
同考試官教諭楊批：說字書作於古，變於後，至我朝而歸於正，明白詳悉，是用錄出。
同考試官教諭胡批：書學切於日用，而學者漫不之省。此篇自源徂委，考究精詳，亦博雅之士也。
考試官侍講張批：通篇文有氣槩，不獨取其記憶而已。
考試官學士梁批：字書源委，考論精切，他卷罕及也。

考書學之繁，而嗟後世之變古；考字體之
translation_en:
…what a novice in learning can fully comprehend. Nevertheless, although the teachings of Cheng and Zhu were alike, why did some of Master Cheng’s disciples drift into Chan Buddhist learning? It was because their abilities and discernment were outstanding and acute, and they often went too far in pursuing what was lofty and remote. Master Zhu also said that they saw only the upper portion of the principles and lacked solid practical effort below. Hence these were the abuses that arose among their later followers. Among Confucius’s disciples, Zengzi alone, despite his slowness, received the responsibility for transmitting the Way: there was indeed good reason for this! These are merely my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. I would be most fortunate if you would instruct me.

Fifth Question
Li Xi 李錫

Comment by Associate Examiner Ren, Instructor: Many candidates in the examination hall could not answer the question on the study of writing. This policy essay explains the subject clearly and almost exhaustively, and its literary vigor is extraordinary. Admirable, admirable!

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: It explains clearly and comprehensively how character dictionaries originated in antiquity, changed in later times, and returned to correctness under our dynasty. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The study of writing is intimately connected with daily use, yet scholars carelessly fail to examine it. This essay investigates the subject precisely and thoroughly, from its origins through its subsequent development. Its author is indeed a man of broad learning and refinement.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Expositor: The writing has vigor and breadth throughout. It is not merely for the author’s powers of recall that I select it.

Comment by Examiner Liang, Academician: Its investigation and discussion of the origins and development of character dictionaries are precise and pertinent. Few other papers equal it.

Examining the complexity of the study of writing, I lament how later ages altered ancient practices; examining character forms and their…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
正而頌
昭代之同文甚矣書學之有關於世道也其
來尚矣古文之變於後世者固不可復而
字體之正於
今日者又豈可以不講哉請因明問而詳言
之字之為用也備萬物之情發三才之蘊
大而聖賢之經訓國家之典章寓焉小而
郡縣之簿書閭閻之契約存焉其有關於
世也豈細故哉粤自結繩政罷書契教興
===
伏羲獲景龍而作龍書黃帝因嘉禾而作
穗書蒼頡觀鳥獸之迹而制字名為科斗
書是則黃帝之先已有字書矣蒼頡之初
作書也依類以象形故謂之文其後形聲
相益即謂之字字者孳乳而寖多也著於
竹帛則謂之書書者如也如其事也是則
三者雖同而義各有取也六書之名起於
周禮一曰象形者隨體詰曲畫成其形日
月之類是也二曰會意者比類合誼以見
punctuated: 正而頌昭代之同文。甚矣，書學之有關於世道也！其來尚矣。古文之變於後世者，固不可復；而字體之正於今日者，又豈可以不講哉？請因明問而詳言之。字之為用也，備萬物之情，發三才之蘊，大而聖賢之經訓、國家之典章寓焉，小而郡縣之簿書、閭閻之契約存焉。其有關於世也，豈細故哉？粤自結繩政罷，書契教興，伏羲獲景龍而作龍書，黃帝因嘉禾而作穗書，蒼頡觀鳥獸之迹而制字，名為科斗書。是則黃帝之先，已有字書矣。蒼頡之初作書也，依類以象形，故謂之文；其後形聲相益，即謂之字。字者，孳乳而寖多也。著於竹帛，則謂之書。書者，如也，如其事也。是則三者雖同，而義各有取也。六書之名起於《周禮》。一曰象形者，隨體詰曲，畫成其形，日月之類是也。二曰會意者，比類合誼，以見
translation_en:
…the correctness of character forms, and praise the uniformity of writing under our illustrious dynasty. Profound indeed is the connection between the study of writing and the moral order of the world! Its origins are ancient. Ancient writing, transformed in later ages, certainly cannot be restored; yet how could we neglect to study the correct character forms established today? Allow me to explain in detail in response to your illuminating question. Written characters encompass the attributes of all things and disclose the hidden workings of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. On the grand scale, they embody the canonical teachings of sages and worthies and the state's statutes and institutions; on the small scale, they preserve prefectural and county registers and the contracts of ordinary households. Can their bearing upon the world be a minor matter?

When government by knotted cords ceased and instruction through written records arose, Fu Xi obtained an auspicious dragon and created dragon script; the Yellow Emperor, inspired by auspicious grain, created grain-ear script; and Cang Jie observed the tracks of birds and beasts and fashioned characters, called tadpole script. Thus, written characters already existed before the Yellow Emperor. When Cang Jie first created writing, he depicted forms according to their categories; hence these were called wen, graphic forms. Later, when form and sound supplemented one another, they were called zi, characters. Zi means that they reproduce and gradually multiply. When inscribed on bamboo and silk, they are called shu, writing. Shu means ru, “to resemble”: writing resembles the matters it records. Thus, although these three refer to the same thing, each designation derives from a distinct meaning.

The designation “Six Principles of Writing” originates in the Rites of Zhou. The first is pictographic representation: following an object's contours and curves, one draws its form. Characters such as “sun” and “moon” are examples. The second is combining meanings: juxtaposing categories and joining their meanings to reveal…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
指撝武信之類是也三曰諧聲者以物爲
聲諧和而成江河之類是也四曰指事者
視而可識察而可見上下之類是也五曰
轉注者建類一首同意相受考老之類是
也六曰假借者本無其字依聲託事令長
之類是也六書之中象形指事爲一耦會
意諧聲爲一耦轉注假借爲一耦此許氏
說文之言也六書起於象形形不可象則
屬諸事事不可指則屬諸意意不可會則
===
屬諸聲四者不足而後轉注假借生焉此
鄭氏相乃之說也蒼頡古文之後至周宣
王時史籀作大篆十五篇與古文或同或
異今石鼓之遺文是已秦始皇時李斯取
籀文而省改之謂之小篆程邈又去繁趨
約施於徒隸謂之隸書古文由此而不傳
矣至於漢魏李唐其體益繁八分書者王
次仲所作蓋割程隸八分而取其二又割
李篆二分而取其八也楷書者鍾繇所作
punctuated:
指撝，武、信之類是也。三曰諧聲者，以物爲聲，諧和而成，江、河之類是也。四曰指事者，視而可識，察而可見，上、下之類是也。五曰轉注者，建類一首，同意相受，考、老之類是也。六曰假借者，本無其字，依聲託事，令、長之類是也。六書之中，象形、指事爲一耦，會意、諧聲爲一耦，轉注、假借爲一耦。此許氏《說文》之言也。六書起於象形，形不可象則屬諸事，事不可指則屬諸意，意不可會則屬諸聲，四者不足而後轉注、假借生焉。此鄭氏相乃之說也。

蒼頡古文之後，至周宣王時，史籀作大篆十五篇，與古文或同或異，今石鼓之遺文是已。秦始皇時，李斯取籀文而省改之，謂之小篆。程邈又去繁趨約，施於徒隸，謂之隸書。古文由此而不傳矣。至於漢、魏、李唐，其體益繁。八分書者，王次仲所作，蓋割程隸八分而取其二，又割李篆二分而取其八也。楷書者，鍾繇所作，
translation_en:
…the intended meaning, as in characters such as wu 武 (“martial”) and xin 信 (“trustworthiness”). Third is phonetic harmonization: a thing supplies the sound, and the character is formed through harmonization, as in jiang 江 and he 河 (“river”). Fourth is indicating matters: the meaning can be recognized by looking and discerned through inspection, as in shang 上 (“above”) and xia 下 (“below”). Fifth is transferred glossing: a category is established under a single head, and characters of the same meaning explain one another, as in kao 考 and lao 老 (“aged”). Sixth is borrowing: where originally there was no character for something, an existing character is borrowed according to its sound to represent it, as in ling 令 (“command”) and chang 長 (“long”). Among the Six Principles of Writing, pictographs and indicators of matters form one pair; combined meanings and phonetic harmonization form another; and transferred glossing and borrowing form the third. This is what Master Xu says in Explaining Graphs (Shuowen). The Six Principles begin with pictographs. When a form cannot be depicted, recourse is made to matters; when matters cannot be indicated, recourse is made to meanings; when meanings cannot be combined, recourse is made to sounds. Only when these four are insufficient do transferred glossing and borrowing arise. This is the explanation of Master Zheng Xiangnai [?].

After Cangjie’s ancient script, in the time of King Xuan of Zhou, the Scribe Zhou composed fifteen chapters in the large-seal script, sometimes agreeing with the ancient script and sometimes differing from it. The surviving inscriptions on the Stone Drums are examples of this. In the time of the First Emperor of Qin, Li Si took Zhou’s script and simplified and modified it; this was called small-seal script. Cheng Miao further eliminated complexity in favor of simplicity and put it to use among convict laborers; this was called clerical script. From this point onward, the ancient script ceased to be transmitted. By the Han, Wei, and Tang of the Li house, the styles had grown increasingly numerous. Eight-part script was created by Wang Cizhong: he supposedly removed eight parts of Cheng’s clerical script and retained two, while removing two parts of Li’s seal script and retaining eight. Regular script was created by Zhong Yao …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
又□□□□行書者潁川劉德升所作章
草者黃門令史游所作飛白者蔡邕見施
堊而作此皆字體之變也雖其源流皆
出於六書未嘗無可取者而古文豈可復
見哉迨至後世承訛襲舛漫無校正偏傍
點畫率意增減而體字益壞矣我
太祖高皇帝一統天下大同文教於是命儒臣
宋濂等取許氏說文與毛晃父子之註釋
勒成洪武正韻一書頒行天下其正字之
===
從俗則如黽俗作黾畫俗作晝雙俗作双
之類是也其正字之所非則如羣作群非
養作𦍒非棗作栆非之類是也其正字之
疑誤則如支攴毋母夲本商啇戌戍戊戎
之類是也百餘年來書學一新然而傳習
既久誠糾亦尠彼府史胥徒皆知遵式而
經生儒士或反不達豈非以報章奏疏者
必經
御覽而窮居巷處者得以苟且自便乎雖然考
punctuated: 又□□□□。行書者，潁川劉德升所作；章草者，黃門令史游所作；飛白者，蔡邕見施堊而作。此皆字體之變也。雖其源流皆出於六書，未嘗無可取者，而古文豈可復見哉？迨至後世，承訛襲舛，漫無校正，偏傍點畫率意增減，而體字益壞矣。我太祖高皇帝一統天下，大同文教，於是命儒臣宋濂等取許氏《說文》與毛晃父子之註釋，勒成《洪武正韻》一書，頒行天下。其正字之從俗，則如黽俗作黾、畫俗作晝、雙俗作双之類是也；其正字之所非，則如羣作群非、養作𦍒非、棗作栆非之類是也；其正字之疑誤，則如支攴、毋母、夲本、商啇、戌戍戊戎之類是也。百餘年來，書學一新。然而傳習既久，誠糾亦尠。彼府史胥徒皆知遵式，而經生儒士或反不達，豈非以報章奏疏者必經御覽，而窮居巷處者得以苟且自便乎？雖然，考
translation_en:
…Furthermore, □□□□ [four illegible characters]. Running script was created by Liu Desheng of Yingchuan; draft cursive script by Shi You, Director of the Palace Gates; and “flying white” script by Cai Yong after he saw whitewash being applied. These are all transformations of the forms of characters. Although their origins all derive from the Six Principles of Writing, and they certainly have their merits, how could the ancient script be seen again? In later ages, errors were perpetuated and mistaken forms inherited, with no systematic correction. Components, dots, and strokes were added or removed at whim, and character forms became increasingly corrupted.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao unified all under Heaven and brought broad uniformity to literary instruction. He therefore commanded the Confucian court official Song Lian and others to draw upon Master Xu’s Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters (Shuowen), together with the annotations of Mao Huang and his son, to compile the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun), which was promulgated throughout the empire. In standardizing characters, it sometimes accepted customary forms: for example, 黽 was commonly written 黾, 畫 was commonly written 晝 [?], and 雙 was commonly written 双. It rejected other forms: for example, writing 羣 as 群, 養 as 𦍒, or 棗 as 栆 was deemed incorrect. It also addressed forms liable to confusion or error, such as 支 and 攴, 毋 and 母, 夲 and 本, 商 and 啇, and 戌, 戍, 戊, and 戎.
For more than a hundred years, the study of writing has been renewed. Yet, as these practices have been transmitted and learned over a long period, corrections have also become rare [?]. Storehouse keepers, scribes, clerks, and runners all know to follow the prescribed forms, while students of the Classics and Confucian scholars sometimes fail to understand them. Is this not because written reports and memorials must pass before the emperor’s eyes, whereas those dwelling in obscure lanes can carelessly follow their own convenience? Nevertheless, the regulation of writing…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
文固
國家之大權而奉行者有司之職務也使違
式自便者皆繩以法則字體之復正不難
矣子思曰今天下車同軌書同文行同倫
愚請以是爲
當代頌孔子曰愚而好自用賤而好自專如
此者烖及其身者也愚請以是爲不恪者
懲且以爲有司之厲焉謹對
punctuated: 文固國家之大權，而奉行者有司之職務也。使違式自便者皆繩以法，則字體之復正不難矣。子思曰：「今天下車同軌，書同文，行同倫。」愚請以是爲當代頌。孔子曰：「愚而好自用，賤而好自專，如此者烖及其身者也。」愚請以是爲不恪者懲，且以爲有司之厲焉。謹對。
translation_en: … the regulation of writing is certainly a major prerogative of the state, while carrying it out is the duty of the responsible officials. If all who disregard the prescribed forms for their own convenience are brought under the discipline of the law, restoring correct character forms will not be difficult. Zisi said: “Today, throughout the realm, carriages have the same wheel gauge, writing uses the same characters, and conduct follows the same norms.” I humbly ask to offer these words in praise of the present age. Confucius said: “Those who are ignorant yet fond of following their own judgment, or of low station yet fond of acting on their own authority—such people bring calamity upon themselves.” I humbly ask that these words serve as a warning to those who fail to observe the rules, and also as an admonition to the responsible officials. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄後序
弘治十四年秋八月壬子
上命學士臣儲侍講臣澯主考順天
府鄉試臣等內顧兢惕罔知所
措越明日
陛辭旣入院三試自甲寅至癸酉
凡二十日而試錄成臣儲旣鋪
===
張揚厲而獻言於
上矣臣不佞僭爲三重之說附於末
簡以終其意而勗於多士曰凡
天子所以輟
帷幄侍從之臣而使主文柄于兹
者無他焉重邦畿之士也凡臣
等所以夙夜從事惟公惟慎而
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄後序

弘治十四年秋八月壬子，上命學士臣儲、侍講臣澯主考順天府鄉試。臣等內顧兢惕，罔知所措。越明日，陛辭，旣入院，三試自甲寅至癸酉，凡二十日，而試錄成。臣儲旣鋪張揚厲而獻言於上矣。臣不佞，僭爲三重之說，附於末簡，以終其意而勗於多士，曰：凡天子所以輟帷幄侍從之臣而使主文柄于兹者，無他焉，重邦畿之士也。凡臣等所以夙夜從事，惟公惟慎而
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

On the renzi day of the eighth month, in autumn of the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, His Majesty commanded your servant Chu 儲, Academician, and your servant Can 澯, Expositor, to serve as chief examiners for the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination. Looking within ourselves, we felt anxious and apprehensive, not knowing how to proceed. The following day, we took our leave of His Majesty and entered the examination compound. The three examination sessions extended from the jiayin day to the guiyou day, twenty days in all, and the examination record was completed. Your servant Chu has already set forth its significance with eloquence and praise and presented his words to His Majesty. Though lacking in ability, I venture to offer an account of three things to be held in esteem, appending it to the final pages to complete his meaning and exhort the many candidates, as follows:

The Son of Heaven releases ministers who attend him in his inner councils from their duties and entrusts them here with authority over literary selection for no other reason than that he holds the scholars of the capital region in esteem. We, his servants, attend to our duties morning and night, intent upon impartiality and care, and …

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不遑寧處者無他焉重
天子之命也然則諸士之登名於錄
者固非尋常遭遇之榮矣而可
不知所重乎夫天下之士皆王
臣也何獨至於邦畿而加重焉
臣固曰謂其爲根本都會之區
也謂
===
王敎之所優渥也謂四方之所則效
也而臣等奉
命而來者亦豈尋常委任之比哉
蓋嘗仰而思俯而惕曰受錢穀
之寄者猶出納之必謹司刑獄
之責者且聽斷之必明況賢材
首務也而又重以
punctuated: 不遑寧處者，無他焉，重天子之命也。然則諸士之登名於錄者，固非尋常遭遇之榮矣，而可不知所重乎？夫天下之士皆王臣也，何獨至於邦畿而加重焉？臣固曰：謂其爲根本都會之區也，謂王敎之所優渥也，謂四方之所則效也。而臣等奉命而來者，亦豈尋常委任之比哉？蓋嘗仰而思，俯而惕，曰：受錢穀之寄者，猶出納之必謹；司刑獄之責者，且聽斷之必明；況賢材，首務也，而又重以
translation_en: …and have had no leisure to rest for no other reason than that we hold the Son of Heaven’s command in high regard. Thus, for the scholars whose names appear in this record, the honor of this opportunity is assuredly no ordinary one. Can they fail to understand what they should hold in high regard? All scholars throughout the realm are subjects of the sovereign. Why, then, are those of the capital region accorded particular importance? Your servant would answer: because this is the region of the realm’s foundation and its capital; because it receives the abundant benefits of royal instruction; and because it is what the four quarters take as their model. And can the charge entrusted to us, who have come in obedience to the imperial command, be compared to an ordinary appointment? Often we have looked upward in reflection and bowed our heads in apprehension, saying: those entrusted with money and grain must be scrupulous in receiving and disbursing them; those responsible for penal cases must be discerning in hearing and deciding them. How much more so when securing worthy talent is the foremost task, and when it is further invested with the weight of…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
天子之命哉此其所以夙夜公愼不
敢怠遑者亦求無負焉耳夫
天子以畿士爲重主司旣敬承之矣
彼其受
恩而思報者宜何說諸士於此蓋
有心之所同然而未能出諸口
者臣能爲之言天之生材也固
===
未嘗擇地而
聖化所被者恒必自近而及遠地氣
之盛者亦必自北而後南凡余
小子幸生
輦轂之下畿甸之間其所以得於
氣化觀感之先者固非若窮鄕
下邑之士引領企足而幸觀光
punctuated:
天子之命哉！此其所以夙夜公愼、不敢怠遑者，亦求無負焉耳。夫天子以畿士爲重，主司旣敬承之矣，彼其受恩而思報者，宜何說？諸士於此，蓋有心之所同然而未能出諸口者，臣能爲之言：
天之生材也，固未嘗擇地，而聖化所被者，恒必自近而及遠；地氣之盛者，亦必自北而後南。凡余小子，幸生輦轂之下、畿甸之間，其所以得於氣化觀感之先者，固非若窮鄕下邑之士，引領企足而幸觀光
translation_en:
…the command of the Son of Heaven! This is why we have remained impartial and vigilant day and night, daring neither to slacken nor to take our ease: we seek only not to fail that trust. Since the Son of Heaven places such importance on the scholars of the metropolitan region, and the examiners have reverently undertaken their charge, what should those who receive his grace and wish to repay it say? On this matter, the scholars surely share a conviction in their hearts that they have not yet been able to voice. Your servant can speak for them:
Heaven has never confined the talents it brings forth to any particular place. Yet the influence of the sage ruler’s transforming instruction invariably spreads from nearby places to distant ones; the flourishing of the earth’s vital energies likewise proceeds from north to south. All of us younger men have had the good fortune to be born beneath the imperial carriage, within the metropolitan region. Our early advantages in receiving these transforming influences and being inspired by what we observe are surely unlike the circumstances of scholars in remote villages and humble towns, who crane their necks and stand on tiptoe, hoping for the good fortune of beholding the imperial splendor…

title: 弘治十四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
於
上國者之難也平居頗以國士自
許皆曰吾欲云云今旣登名於
錄將嚮用矣亦孰肯自負所學
而甘爲人下耶惟其不自負也
而後爲知所重知所重則今日
朝廷之眷注與主司之掄選皆不
===
失其重矣一舉而三重備焉顧
不韙歟不然則是錄之名異日
指而議之者衆矣嗚呼可不勉
哉可不懼哉
翰林院侍講張爘謹序
punctuated:
於上國者之難也。平居頗以國士自許，皆曰：「吾欲云云。」今旣登名於錄，將嚮用矣，亦孰肯自負所學，而甘爲人下耶？惟其不自負也，而後爲知所重。知所重，則今日朝廷之眷注與主司之掄選，皆不失其重矣。一舉而三重備焉，顧不韙歟？不然，則是錄之名，異日指而議之者衆矣。嗚呼！可不勉哉？可不懼哉？

翰林院侍講張爘謹序。
translation_en:
…in the imperial capital face such difficulty. In ordinary life, you have prided yourselves on being men of outstanding ability, all saying, “I aspire to do such and such.” Now that your names have been entered in this record and you are about to be entrusted with service, who would willingly betray his own learning and resign himself to being inferior to others? Only by not betraying yourselves can you be said to understand what deserves weight. If you understand this, then neither the court’s attentive regard today nor the chief examiners’ selection will lose its weight. In this one undertaking, all three forms of weight are fulfilled—is this not fitting? Otherwise, in days to come, many will point to the names in this record and criticize them. Alas! Can you fail to exert yourselves? Can you fail to feel apprehension?

Respectfully prefaced by Zhang Can 張爘, Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
